title: Jap - Discrimination Against Third Party Nationals In Occupied Areas

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,
APR 1 4 1939
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. 3. B. D.）

1938 Difficulties Are Reviewed In Report Of British Commerce Group

Restrictions On Trade As Result Of Hostilities Are Emphasized; Interference With Currency In North China And Closure Of Important Rivers

DISCRIMINATION AGAINST THIRD PARTY NATIONALS IN OCCUPIED AREAS

The annual meetings of the British Chamber of Commerce and China Association were held at the Shanghai Club last evening when Sir Robert Calder-Marshall gave a comprehensive survey of conditions throughout China, as they affected British traders and business during 1938. Emphasis was placed on the continued restrictions on trading of third party nationals in the occupied areas and the discriminatory treatment accorded neutral citizens. The interference with Chinese currency in North China and the closure to third party shipping of important rivers also came in for condemnation by the Chairman of the Chamber.

Speakers at the meetings were Sir Robert Calder-Marshall, Mr. A. H. George and Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead.

Among those present were: Sir Herbert Phillips, K.C.M.G., D.B.E., H.B.M. Consul-General and Honorary President of the Chamber, Mr. A. H. George, C.M.G., Commercial Counsellor and Honorary Vice-President of the Chamber, Sir Robert Calder-Marshall, K.B.E., Chairman of the Chamber; Mr. C. H. Arnold, Vice-Chairman; Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead, C.B.E., Chairman of the China Association; Mr. J. R. Jones, M.C., Vice-Chairman; Mr. H. F. Baker, M.B.E. Secretary; Mr. V. O. Riley, Assistant Secretary, and a number of members of both organisations.

Sir Robert Calder-Marshall said:
The work of the Chamber during 1938 has naturally been mainly concerned with problems arising out of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, not only in Shanghai but in the hinterland of Shanghai, the Yangtze Valley and North China, conditions in which areas seriously affect the interests and trade of this port.

Ports Occupied
During the year under review, though there have been no actual hostilities in Shanghai, there have been continuous military operations on all fronts which resulted in the occupation of Amoy in May and the fall of Canton and Hankow in October, thus placing Japanese troops in occupation, though not in control, of a large part of North Central and South China including the most important ports and commercial marts, and depriving the National Government of the immediate use of the major part of the revenue derived from the Customs.

These operations have led to the creation of regulations which restrict trade and commerce and which are in some cases, as in Tsingtao and the Yangtze, discriminatory against third power nationals, which judging from the brief telegraphic resume of the report of the Central China Development Co. the establishment of monopolies in certain lines of endeavour is already an accomplished fact.

With the renewal of hostilities from the Shanghai area it might have been anticipated that the restrictions imposed on freedom of ingress and egress for Chinese goods and persons from the Northern and Eastern districts would have been withdrawn and that the re-establishment of industry in these areas by Chinese might have been encouraged, but instead of this being the case, twelve months since active hostilities were being waged in Shanghai restrictions are still imposed on entry of Chinese to the Northern and Eastern districts, and it has not been possible for Chinese industry to be re-established in the districts while the British owned Tram and Bus Companies, which hold a franchise from the Municipal Council, are unable to operate though a Japanese Bus Company is operating north of the creek without any legal right.

Confidence Destroyed
Delay in the restoration of these districts to municipal administration and the continuance of military restrictions destroy that confidence which is or should be the desire of all to engender.

Shanghai is dependent for her trade on freedom of access to the hinterland, to the Yangtze Valley and Szechwan and to Northern ports, and any obstructions to these channels of trade are of vital importance to her. The war very naturally placed impediments in the way of trade, but neither "military necessity" nor solicitude for the welfare of foreign shipping can now be accepted as valid reasons for the complete closure of the river to foreign merchant vessels, as for some time past Japanese merchant vessels have been transporting commercial cargo to and from river ports and Japanese transportation companies have even advertised in the Chinese press their readiness to accept and transport cargo to the interior, while Japanese and Sino-Japanese transportation hongs have been established at river ports.

The matter is of vital importance to British traders and British shipping, both trade and shipping being temporarily immobilised while the Japanese are, for the time being, monopolizing Yangtze trade and transport. This closure of the river to foreign shipping, other than Japanese, is also of serious moment to foreigners who are marooned in Hankow and who, through lack of accommodation on Japanese vessels, cannot be relieved.

No Solution Seen
Representations have been made and will continue to be made but as far the Japanese do not appear to realise their obligations to third party nationals and no satisfactory solution is in sight at the moment.

《字林西报》，
1939年4月14日
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 S. B. 登记号 3. B. D.）

英国商业团体报告回顾1938年的困难

强调敌对行动导致的贸易限制；华北货币受干扰及重要河流封闭

占领区内对第三国国民的歧视

昨晚，英国商会和中国协会在上海总会举行年度会议，罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士（Sir Robert Calder-Marshall）全面综述了1938年间影响英国商人和商业的中国各地局势。会议重点强调了在占领区内继续限制第三国国民的贸易以及对中立国公民的歧视性待遇。商会主席还谴责了在华北干扰中国货币以及禁止第三国船只进入重要河流的行为。

会议发言人有：罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士、A. H. 乔治先生（Mr. A. H. George）和 H. G. W. 伍德黑德先生（Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead）。

出席者包括：赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips），K.C.M.G., D.B.E.，英国驻华总领事兼商会名誉主席；A. H. 乔治先生，C.M.G.，商务参赞兼商会名誉副主席；罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士，K.B.E.，商会主席；C. H. 阿诺德先生（Mr. C. H. Arnold），副主席；H. G. W. 伍德黑德先生，C.B.E.，中国协会主席；J. R. 琼斯先生（Mr. J. R. Jones），M.C.，副主席；H. F. 贝克先生（Mr. H. F. Baker），M.B.E.，秘书；V. O. 莱利先生（Mr. V. O. Riley），助理秘书，以及两个组织的众多会员。

罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士说：
1938年商会的工作自然主要关注因中日敌对行动而产生的问题，这不仅涉及上海，还包括上海腹地、长江流域和华北地区，这些地区的状况严重影响了本港的利益和贸易。

港口被占领
在回顾的这一年中，虽然上海没有发生实际的敌对行动，但各战线持续进行军事行动，导致5月厦门被占领，10月广州和汉口陷落，从而使日军占领（虽非完全控制）了华中、华北和华南的大部分地区，包括最重要的港口和商业中心，并剥夺了国民政府对大部分关税收入的即时使用权。

这些行动导致了限制贸易和商业的法规的产生，在某些情况下，如在青岛和长江，这些法规对第三强国国民具有歧视性。根据华中开发公司报告的简要电文摘要判断，在某些行业建立垄断已成为既成事实。

随着上海地区战事重开，人们原本可能预期，针对中国货物和人员从北部和东部地区进出的自由所施加的限制会被取消，并且可能会鼓励中国人在这些地区重建工业。但事实并非如此，在上海发生积极敌对行动十二个月后的今天，中国人进入北部和东部地区仍受到限制，中国人无法在这些地区重建工业，而拥有工部局特许经营权的英资电车和巴士公司无法运营，尽管一家日资巴士公司在毫无法律依据的情况下在苏州河以北运营。

信心遭破坏
这些地区恢复市政管理的延误以及军事限制的持续，破坏了所有人希望培养或本应培养的信心。

上海的贸易依赖于自由进入腹地、长江流域、四川以及北方港口，任何对这些贸易通道的阻碍对其都至关重要。战争自然给贸易设置了障碍，但现在无论是“军事需要”还是对外国航运福利的关切，都不能再被视为完全关闭河流禁止外国商船通行的正当理由，因为一段时间以来，日本商船一直在向河流港口往返运输商业货物，日本运输公司甚至在中国报纸上刊登广告，表示愿意接受并运输货物到内地，而且在河流港口已经建立了日资和中日合资的运输行。

此事对英国商人和英国航运业至关重要，目前贸易和航运暂时陷入停滞，而日本人则暂时垄断了长江的贸易和运输。除日本船只外，禁止其他外国船只进入河流，对于那些被困在汉口、因日本船只舱位不足而无法撤离的外国人来说，也事关重大。

未见解决方案
已提出交涉并将继续提出交涉，但截至目前，日本人似乎并未意识到其对第三国国民的义务，目前看来没有令人满意的解决方案。

themselves of British tonnage.
The monopolization of the inland
water transportation by the Japan-
ese has an important effect upon
British trade as it places all Chin-
ese inland water transport under
Japanese control and is thus in a
position to apply discriminatory
measures, while of course it is in
direct contravention of Treaty rights
enjoyed by British.

Imports And Exports
For purpose of record the follow-
ing comparative figures for trade
are given:—
1936
Imports into Shanghai .... 553,094,903
Exports from Shanghai .... 361,400,621
1937
Imports into Shanghai .... 508,944,132
Exports from Shanghai .... 404,395,418
1938
Imports into Shanghai .... 269,092,315
Exports from Shanghai .... 222,181,071
These figures are however some-
what misleading as it must be re-
cognized that the early months of
1938 included and practically con-
sisted of goods which had been re-
shipped from other ports, where
they had been landed as "deviated"
cargo and which would normally
have appeared in the 1937 imports.
Trade in general cannot be re-
garded as healthy or the outlook as
promising for the immediate future,
for until the normal channels of
trade are free imports and exports
must suffer restrictions.
On June 1 a new Customs tariff
was promulgated by the Provisional
Government of North China and
Reformed Government effective in
Japanese occupied territories, the
rates in general being those of the
tariff of 1931, though in some cases
the rates were lower than 1931.

Industry In 1938
One of the main features of 1938
was the establishment of a large
number of industrial plants in the
Western area demonstrating the
courage and determination of the
Chinese industrialist, who having
lost his plant in the Yangtsepo or
other industrial centres did not
hesitate to start again in an area
where he felt he would be safe
from interference. Though many of
the plants are small and would, in
normal times, be uneconomic they
have for the most part done well
and will doubtless be extended and
become firmly established.
Important industrial plants of
Chinese ownership in the Eastern
district have for the most part been
either destroyed or looted or, if in
operation, are not under the con-
trol of their original owners, while
in such areas as Wusih and Chang-
chow, which were formerly im-
portant centres of industry, it is
understood that much of the
machinery which had not been de-
stroyed has been removed.

致使中国托运人无法
利用英国的吨位。
日本人对内河运输的垄断
对英国贸易有重要影响，因为它
将所有中国内河运输置于
日本控制之下，从而能够
实施歧视性措施，这当然
直接违反了英国享有的条约权利。

进出口
为记录起见，列出以下贸易
比较数据：—
1936年
上海进口 ____ 553,094,903
上海出口 ____ 361,400,621
1937年
上海进口 ____ 508,944,132
上海出口 ____ 404,395,418
1938年
上海进口 ____ 269,092,315
上海出口 ____ 222,181,071
然而，这些数字有些
误导性，因为必须认识到，1938年
初几个月包含且实际上主要由
从其他港口转运的货物组成，这些
货物作为“改道”货物在那里卸货，
正常情况下应出现在1937年的进口
统计中。总体而言，贸易状况不能
被视为健康，近期前景也不容乐观，
因为在正常贸易通道畅通之前，
进出口必然受到限制。
6月1日，华北临时政府和
维新政府颁布了新海关税则，在
日本占领区生效，税率大体上
采用1931年税则，尽管在某些
情况下税率低于1931年。

1938年的工业
1938年的主要特征之一是在
西部地区建立了大量工厂，这显
示了中国实业家的勇气和决心，
他们在杨树浦或其他工业中心
失去工厂后，毫不犹豫地在一个
他们认为可以免受干扰的地区
重新开始。虽然许多工厂规模
较小，在正常时期可能不经济，
但它们大多经营良好，无疑将
会扩展并稳固立足。
东部地区重要的华资工厂大
多已被摧毁或掠夺，或者即便在
运营，也不在原业主的控制之
下，而在无锡和常州等以前重
要的工业中心，据悉许多未被
摧毁的机器设备已被搬走。

Cargo At Wharves
At the last annual meeting refer-
ence was made to the cargo lying
at the Japanese Wharves and at the
Wharves of the China Merchants
Steam Navigation Company, release
of which had been delayed on ac-
count of the hostilities. It is satis-
factory to record that the bulk of
the cargo has now been delivered
to its legal owners; however, as re-
gards the cargo at the China Mer-
chants' Wharves, though when the
Cargo Removal Committee, ap-
pointed by the Japanese to attend
to the removal of cargo, was dis-
banded at the end of December it
was stated that all cargo at the
wharves had been delivered, in fact
a considerable amount of cargo is
still undelivered and unaccounted
for and should be at the wharves.
In as much as both the Central
Wharf and Lower Wharf have been
in the hands of the Japanese Mili-
tary or Naval authorities ever since
the commencement of hostilities, it
is obvious that neither guerrillas
nor refugees could have had a hand
in the disappearance of the cargo.
This is obviously a case in which
the Japanese authorities are direct-
ly responsible and in connection
with which the legal owners of the
goods should be immediately reim-
bursed for the value of the goods
which have been illegally removed
while Japanese authorities were in
occupation of the wharves and
should be regarded as an entirely
different category from ordinary
"war claims."

Customs Revenues And Loans
In May 1938 arrangements were
made between the Japanese and
British Governments whereby Cus-
toms Revenues collected at the
occupied ports should be deposited
with the Yokohama Specie Bank in
the name of the Inspector-General
of Customs and that such part of
these funds as were needed for the
service of the Foreign Loans should
be released as required. The agree-
ment also provided for the release
to Japan of certain funds held by
the Chinese National Government.
Inasmuch as the National Govern-
ment of China was not a party to
the arrangement and did not give
approval to it, the agreement has
not been implemented in so far as
the release of funds to meet foreign
obligations is concerned though the
Customs revenues collected in
occupied territory are being de-
posited with the Yokohama Specie
Bank.
The National Government, never-
theless, met, from other sources, all
foreign Loan obligations up to
December 31, 1938, when it issued
a notice stating that from January
1, 1939 it could no longer meet the
obligations in full but would de-
posit with the Central Bank of
China the quota for the loans
which would be payable from the
revenues of the ports still under
its control.
It is to be hoped that the Chin-
ese Government will give its ap-
proval to the arrangement and thus
prevent default on its foreign loan
obligations.

Railways Occupied
Resulting from the advances made
by the Japanese forces, all the im-
portant railways of China are now
in their hands. These railways were
built with funds borrowed abroad
and are hypothecated as security for
the loans. The revenues of these
railways are now being used by the
Japanese authorities for their own
purposes and no provision is being
made for the service of the loans.
The Chinese Government has pro-
tested against this action but so far
without result. It is hoped that the
Japanese authorities will realize
the injustice of their action and
make provision for the service of
the loans.

码头货物
在上次年度会议上，曾提及
堆放在日本码头和招商局码头
的货物，其放行因敌对行动而
延误。令人满意的是，大部分货
物现已交付给合法所有者；然
而，关于招商局码头的货物，尽
管日本任命的负责处理货物搬
运的货物搬运委员会在12月底
解散时声称码头上的所有货物
均已交付，但实际上仍有大量
货物未交付且下落不明，理应
仍在码头上。鉴于自敌对行动
开始以来，中央码头和下码头一
直由日本军方或海军当局控制，
显然游击队或难民不可能参与
货物的失踪。这显然是日本当
局直接负责的案例，与此相关，
货物的合法所有者应立即获得
在日本当局占领码头期间被非
法移走的货物价值的赔偿，此
类赔偿应被视为与普通“战争
索赔”完全不同的类别。

关税收入与借款
1938年5月，日本和英国政
府之间达成协议，规定在被占
领港口征收的关税收入应以海
关总税务司的名义存入横滨正
金银行，并根据需要释放其中用
于偿还外债的部分资金。该协
定还规定向日本释放由中国国
民政府持有的某些资金。由于
中国国民政府并非该协定的一
方，也未批准该协定，因此在释
放资金以履行对外义务方面，
该协定尚未实施，尽管在被占
领土征收的关税收入正存入横
滨正金银行。
尽管如此，国民政府通过其
他来源支付了截至1938年12月
31日的所有外债义务，当时它发
布通知称，从1939年1月1日起，
它不再能全额履行这些义务，但
会将用于偿还贷款的配额存入
中国银行，这部分款项将从其
仍控制的港口收入中支付。
希望中国政府能批准该协
定，从而避免在其外债义务上
违约。

铁路被占领
由于日军的推进，中国所有
重要铁路现在都在其手中。这些
铁路是利用国外借款建造的，
并作为贷款的抵押品。这些铁
路的收入现在被日本当局用于
其自身目的，未做任何安排来
偿还贷款。中国政府已对此行
动提出抗议，但迄今未有结果。
希望日本当局能认识到其行动
的不公正性，并做出安排以偿
还贷款。

03887

page_data.en:
On February 11, 1938. the Federat-
ed Reserve Bank was established
under Japanese auspices in North
China and on March 10, 1938 it com-
menced its issue of notes which
were inadequately backed and
which were not convertible into
free foreign exchange but were
convertible at par with the yen into
legal tender notes of the National
Government possessing foreign ex-
change value. In order to meet the
danger to the National Currency
arising from this move the Chinese
Government on March 13 restricted
the sale of foreign exchange, but
permitted weekly allotments accord-
ing to legitimate trade requirements.
Foreign Exchange
Following the withdrawal by the
Central Bank of China of facilities
for conversion of notes into foreign
exchange the rate of 1/2½ at which
the dollar had been stabilized since
1935 gradually declined to about 8d.
at which level it has been steady
for some time.
On March 11, 1939, regulations
were issued by the Provisional
Government of North China with
the intention of enforcing the use
in North China of the Federated
Reserve Bank notes, which are not
freely convertible into foreign ex-
change and ousting the National
Currency which has definite foreign
exchange value.
To facilitate the carrying out of
this intention the Customs have
been forbidden to permit the ex-
ports of certain goods constituting
the main articles of exports from
North China unless the foreign ex-
change for such shipments is nego-
tiated through the Yokohama
Specie Bank and converted into
F.R.B. currency at the rate of 1/2
per F.R.B. dollar.
This rule automatically estab-
lishes a financial monopoly in
North China in favour of Japanese
Banks, penalizes North China pro-
duce which would be non-competi-
tive and while the regulations will
in the first place be felt by ex-
porters it will soon be felt by im-
porters of foreign goods (other than
Japanese) as there is no guarantee
that such exchange as may become
available from exports will be used
to finance imports.
Trade At Standstill
The regulations are definitely dis-
criminatory and contrary to the
principle of the open door.
The immediate effect of these
regulations has been to bring trade
in the North to a virtual standstill.
In the last annual report it was
stated that "it is realized that far
more important problems may arise
which may tend to deprive us of
"the equal opportunity and the
open door" which we can legitimate-
ly claim as our right." This fore-
cast has been amply justified. Dif-
ficult problems have been and are
now before us.
From reports received from North
and Central China during the past
year and local experience and also
from the report of the Central
China Development Co. it seems
evident that the policy adopted by
Japan is one of exploitation, bene-
ficial to Japan and Japanese
nationals.
The establishment of monopolies,
confiscation or forced co-operation
in industry on terms unfavourable
to the legal owners, discrimination
in favour of Japanese nationals or
Japanese shipping, will not engen-
der that confidence without which
trade, commerce and industry can-
not prosper and lacking which the
pacification of the country districts
cannot be achieved.
Temporarily the outlook for
North and Central China does not
appear bright, but there is no need
for despair, every ill has its anti-
dote, and the time must come when
this struggle will terminate.

1938年2月11日，联合准备银行（Federated Reserve Bank）在日本的扶持下于华北成立，并于1938年3月10日开始发行纸币。这些纸币准备金不足，不能兑换自由外汇，但可按平价兑换成具有外汇价值的国民政府法定货币日元。为了应对此举对法币造成的危险，中国政府于3月13日限制外汇出售，但允许根据正当贸易需求进行每周配给。

外汇
继中国银行停止提供将纸币兑换为外汇的服务后，自1935年以来稳定在1/2½便士的美元汇率逐渐下跌至约8便士，并在此水平上保持了一段时间的稳定。

1939年3月11日，华北临时政府颁布法规，意图在华北强制使用不能自由兑换外汇的联合准备银行纸币，并排挤具有明确外汇价值的法币。

为促进这一意图的实施，海关被禁止允许构成华北主要出口商品的某些货物出口，除非这些货物的外汇通过横滨正金银行交涉，并按每联合准备银行元兑1/2便士的汇率兑换成联合准备银行货币。

此规定自动确立了有利于日本银行的华北金融垄断，惩罚了缺乏竞争力的华北产品。虽然出口商将首先感受到这些法规的影响，但外国商品（日本除外）的进口商很快也会受到影响，因为无法保证从出口中获得的外汇会用于资助进口。

贸易停滞
这些法规显然具有歧视性，且违背门户开放原则。

这些法规的直接影响是使华北贸易几乎陷入停滞。在上一年度报告中曾指出：“人们意识到，可能会出现更为重要的问题，这些问题可能倾向于剥夺我们合法声称有权享有的‘平等机会和门户开放’。”这一预测已得到充分证实。困难的问题已经出现，并且目前正摆在我们面前。

根据过去一年从华北和华中等地收到的报告、本地经验以及华中开发公司的报告，显而易见，日本采取的政策是一种剥削政策，仅有利于日本及其国民。

建立垄断、没收或在不利于合法所有者的条件下强迫工业合作、优待日本国民或日本航运的歧视行为，不会产生贸易、商业和工业繁荣所必需的信任，而缺乏这种信任，乡村地区的安定也无法实现。

暂时看来，华北和华中的前景并不明朗，但无需绝望，每种弊病都有其解药，这场斗争终有结束之时。

02888

page_data.en:
China is predominantly an
agricultural country and though
the industrial life of the cities has
been emphasized and has to a large
extent been destroyed in the in-
vaded areas, the strength of China
lies in the country districts which
in most parts have been unaffect-
ed by the tide of war. The occupa-
tion of the cities though it impedes
commerce and prevents rehabilita-
tion only affects the country dis-
tricts to a minor degree for as was
said in a lecture at Chatham House,
the fighting has been with a "fist
on one side and soft glue on the
other" therefore however, many
cities may be occupied they are
still surrounded by the country-
side.
It is this fact that accounts for
the resilience of the Chinese and
gives ground for belief in a speedy
recovery once the tide of war
passes.
Many Impediments
In the West and Southwest of
China the picture appears brighter.
There we see development pro-
gressing rapidly and a calm quiet
confidence in place of the gloomy
fears expressed in the North.
There is no doubt that the devel-
opment of the Southwest will con-
tinue and that when China
emerges from his struggle it will
be as a greatly strengthened nation.
In order that a true picture of
conditions ruling in 1938 and now
may be presented, it has unfor-
tunately been necessary to refer
to the many impediments which
have been placed in the way of
trade and a return to normal and
sane conditions, and it is sincerely
to be hoped that next year a dif-
ferent and more pleasing picture
may be presented.
It has been said by the Japanese
that we do not understand her in-
tentions, but if those intentions
were directed to good neighbour-
liness I think there would be no
ground for claiming lack of under-
standing on the part of others.
I will now as usual give you a
brief review of the Chamber's work
during last year.
Joint Committee
The Joint Committee held 50 re-
gular meetings during the year.
The number and variety of the
questions discussed at these has
been conveyed to members in the
reports issued from time to time.
A suggestion was made that more
than one general meeting of mem-
bers should be held in each year
so as to give the Committee an
opportunity of reporting on current
problems and on actions taken in
connection with them. It was hop-
ed to hold an extra general meeting
in December, but I regret that
owing chiefly to stress of work
and many other meetings con-
tinually being called it was not
found practicable to do so.
I would like to make it quite
clear that information on all mat-
ters is available to members at
any time on application to the
Secretary, and minutes and docu-
ments in connection with any ques-
tion are open to their confidential
inspection.
In addition to the regular meet-
ings two special meetings were
held on May 19 and December 9.
We were honoured by the presence
of H. M. Ambassador on both occa-
sions and by the attendance of the
Commander-in-Chief at the second
meeting.

02889
page_data.zh:
中国主要是一个农业国家，尽管城市工业生活受到重视，且在沦陷区很大程度上遭到破坏，但中国的力量在于乡村地区，这些地区在大部分地方未受战争浪潮的影响。城市的占领虽然阻碍了商业并妨碍了复兴，但对乡村地区的影响较小，正如在查塔姆研究所（Chatham House）的一次演讲中所说，战斗是一方出“拳头”，另一方出“软胶”，因此，无论多少城市被占领，它们仍然被乡村所包围。

正是这一事实解释了中国人的韧性，并为人们相信一旦战争浪潮过去就能迅速恢复提供了依据。

诸多障碍
在中国西部和西南部，景象显得较为光明。在那里，我们看到发展迅速推进，取代了北部所表达的阴郁恐惧的是一种平静的自信。

毫无疑问，西南的发展将继续下去，当中国从这场斗争中走出来时，它将成为一个大大增强的国家。

为了如实呈现1938年及目前的状况，不幸的是有必要提及那些阻碍贸易回归正常和理智状态的诸多障碍，真诚地希望明年能呈现出一幅不同且更令人愉悦的景象。

日本人曾说我们不理解他们的意图，但如果这些意图旨在睦邻友好，我认为就没有理由声称他人缺乏理解。

现在，我将像往常一样简要回顾本会上一年度的工作。

联合委员会
联合委员会在本年度举行了50次常规会议。会议上讨论的问题的数量和多样性已通过不时发布的报告传达给会员。

有人建议每年举行不止一次会员大会，以便让委员会有机会报告当前问题及为此采取的行动。原希望在12月举行一次额外的大会，但我很遗憾，由于主要工作压力大且不断召开其他会议，发现这样做并不切实可行。

我想明确指出，会员可随时向秘书申请获取所有事项的信息，与任何问题相关的会议记录和文件均可供其保密查阅。

除常规会议外，还于5月19日和12月9日举行了两次特别会议。英国驻华大使荣幸地出席了这两次会议，总司令出席了第二次会议。

02889

page_data.en:
Sub-Committees
The Sub-Committees of the
Chamber have been active during
the year under review and many
meetings were held. The matters
discussed at these meetings have
of necessity been entirely connect-
ed with the problems that have
arisen from the hostilities. Their
deliberations and recommendations
have been of much assistance
to the Joint Committee dur-
ing a difficult time, and
the thanks of the Chamber are
due to the members of all Sub-
Committees for services they have
rendered.

The Language School
The Language School Sub-Com-
mittee had again to face the dif-
ficult problem of trying to place
the School on a self-supporting
basis. The continued loss on the
running of the School is proving
a drain on the Chamber's resources
and has caused your Finance Com-
mittee some concern. It was appar-
ent that the time would come
when there would be no alternative
but to close the School unless it
could be run without further loss.
The whole question was carefully
considered by the Sub-Committee
and the Principal of the School
in the middle of last year. The
Principal very generously agreed
to accept considerably less remu-
neration and the Chinese teachers
also met the situation by consent-
ing to a reduction in their salaries.
This new arrangement came into
force on July 1, and under
it the School could just pay its
way provided an average of 30
students per month was maintain-
ed throughout the year.
It is hoped that there may be
a material increase in the number
of students and thus obviate the
necessity of closing.
The matter has the serious con-
sideration of your Committee
which is desirous of continuing the
School, if possible.
The thanks of the Chamber are
due to Mr. S. G. Beare and Mr
G. W. Creighton for conducting
the Chinese Language examinations
in Shanghai, and to Major G. A.
Herbert, Mr. Allen Price, Mr. K.
W. Tribe, Mr. R. Trounce Nelson,
Mr. G. V. Kitson and Mr. E. B.
Boothby for conducting the ex-
aminations in Tientsin, Hongkong,
Chefoo and Hankow.

Apprenticeship Scheme
The Selection Committee of the
Scheme of Apprenticeships of the
Federation of British Industries
have had a busy year and a record
number of 24 students have been
sent to the United Kingdom for
training in Engineering Works.
These were selected out of 120
applicants and the grading, inter-
viewing, and arranging for medical
examinations, passages, passports,
exchange, etc. have entailed a great
deal of time and work. The Scheme
has become increasingly popular
and it is hoped again this year
firms in Great Britain will offer
vacancies in a variety of different
spheres of engineering activity.

Unemployment Fund
After serious consideration the
Unemployment Fund Sub-Com-
mittee decided to recommend the
reopening of the Fund again last
autumn, but in view of the general
financial stringency it was decided
to limit the appeal to four months
instead of six. The result has
been, as before, a most generous
response, and it has enabled the
Committee to deal with several
cases of repatriation and also to
build up a suitable reserve to
handle future cases and appeals
that may be submitted to them
during the remainder of this year.
The Unemployment Fund Sub-
Committee has continued to work
in close conjunction with the
British Fund for Relief in China.
There has only been one arbitra-
tion during the year and no
surveys were conducted.

小组委员会
在本审查年度内，本会的小组委员会活动频繁，举行了多次会议。这些会议上讨论的事项必然完全源于敌对行动所产生的问题。在困难时期，它们的审议和建议对联合委员会大有裨益，本会谨向所有小组委员会成员提供的服务表示感谢。

语言学校
语言学校小组委员会再次面临试图使学校实现自负盈亏的难题。学校运营的持续亏损正在消耗本会的资源，并引起了财务委员会的一些担忧。显然，除非学校能在不再亏损的情况下运营，否则迟早别无选择，只能关闭。

去年年中，小组委员会和学校校长仔细考虑了整个问题。校长非常慷慨地同意接受大幅减少的报酬，中文教师也通过同意减薪来应对这一局面。这项新安排于7月1日生效，根据该安排，只要全年保持每月平均30名学生，学校就能勉强维持收支平衡。

希望学生人数能有实质性增加，从而避免关闭的必要。

此事已得到委员会的认真考虑，委员会希望能尽可能继续开办该学校。

本会谨感谢 S. G. Beare 先生和 G. W. Creighton 先生在上海主持中文考试，并感谢 G. A. Herbert 少校、Allen Price 先生、K. W. Tribe 先生、R. Trounce Nelson 先生、G. V. Kitson 先生和 E. B. Boothby 先生在天津、香港、烟台和汉口主持考试。

学徒计划
英国工业联合会学徒计划选拔委员会度过了忙碌的一年，创纪录地选派了24名学生前往英国在工程工厂接受培训。这些学生是从120名申请人中选拔出来的，分级、面试以及安排体检、船票、护照、外汇等事宜耗费了大量的时间和精力。该计划越来越受欢迎，希望今年英国的公司能再次在各种不同的工程活动领域提供空缺职位。

失业基金
经过认真考虑，失业基金小组委员会决定建议于去年秋季重新开放该基金，但鉴于普遍的资金紧张，决定将募捐期限制为四个月而非六个月。结果如前所述，响应极为慷慨，这使得委员会能够处理几起遣返案件，并建立适当的储备金，以处理本年度剩余时间内可能提交给他们的未来案件和申请。

失业基金小组委员会继续与英国在华救济基金密切合作。本年度仅进行一次仲裁，未开展任何调查。

The Trade Enquiry Department
has dealt with some 36 enquiries
in 1938 and a number of prospec-
tive buyers and sellers have been
put in touch with each other.
The granting of certificates of
origin to members has also con-
tinued. Including these and other
certificates a total of 75 were issu-
ed last year to members of the
Chamber.
Four volumes of the National Gov-
ernments' Laws and Regulations
were issued during the year, making
a total number of volumes issued
25. These constitute a valuable re-
cord of Laws published by the
Chinese Government, of which
there is no other compilation of
translations in existence. Two fur-
ther volumes are now in course of
preparation and it is hoped they will
be issued during 1939.
Commercial Examinations
Another very active part of the
Chamber's work is the London
Chamber of Commerce Commercial
examinations which are conducted
twice yearly. These examinations
are becoming increasingly popular
and the number of entries is grow-
ing.
The Chamber has received a num-
ber of applications during last year
from British subjects for employ-
ment and by means of the Employ-
ment Register it has been possible
to find positions for a very fair pro-
portion of the applicants.
Secretariat
On November 30 last Miss P. A.
Ayrton retired from secretaryship
of the Chamber after 14 years
loyal service. Her resignation was
accepted with great regret and in
appreciation of the long and valu-
able services rendered by her a
presentation of a canteen of silver
was made to her by our Honorary
President on behalf of the Joint
Committee prior to the regular fort-
nightly meeting of December 2, 1938.
Mr. H. F. Baker was appointed
secretary as from December 1, 1938.
I cannot conclude without men-
tioning the valuable assistance re-
ceived from the Commercial Coun-
sellor, Mr. A. H. George, and from
the Commercial Secretary, Mr. R.
H. Scott, who have both given gen-
erously of their time in attending
Joint and Sub-Committee meetings
and their opinions and advice on
many of the complicated problems
with which we have been confront-
ed has been of the greatest help to
your Committee
In conclusion I would like to ex-
press to Mr. Baker and the staff
our sincere appreciation of their
faithful service during the past
year.
Before submitting the Report and
Accounts, I will ask our Honorary
Vice-President and Commercial
Counsellor, Mr. A. H. George, to
address you.
Mr. A. H. George then addressed
the meeting and spoke on the gen-
eral trading conditions at present
existing in China.
The report and accounts were
adopted on the motion of Sir Robert
Calder-Marshall, seconded by Mr.
C. H. Arnhold.

在1938年处理了约36起查询，

相互联系。
向会员签发原产地证书的工作
也继续进行。包括这些证书及其
他证书在内，去年共向商会会员
签发了75份证书。
本年度出版了四卷《国民政府法
律法规汇编》，使已出版的总卷
数达到25卷。这些构成了中国政
府颁布法律的一份宝贵记录，目
前尚无其他译本汇编存在。另有
两卷正在编纂中，希望能在1939

商业考试
商会工作的另一个非常活跃的部
分是一年举行两次的伦敦商会商
业考试。这些考试越来越受欢迎，
报考人数也在增加。
去年，商会收到了一些英籍人士
的求职申请，通过就业登记册，
已为相当比例的申请人找到了职
位。
秘书处
去年11月30日，P. A. Ayrton小姐
在忠诚服务14年后，辞去了商会
秘书职务。她的辞呈被怀着极大
的遗憾接受；为了感谢她长期以
来提供的宝贵服务，在1938年12
月2日常规双周会议之前，由我们
的名誉主席代表联合委员会向她
赠送了一套银质餐具。
H. F. Baker先生自1938年12月1日
起被任命为秘书。
在结束本报告之前，我必须提及
从商务参赞A. H. George先生和商
务秘书R. H. Scott先生那里获得的
宝贵协助，他们慷慨地抽出时间
参加联合委员会及小组委员会会
议，他们就我们要面对的许多复
杂问题所提出的意见和建议，对
贵委员会帮助极大。
最后，我要向Baker先生及其工作
人员表示诚挚的谢意，感谢他们
在过去一年中的忠实服务。
在提交报告和账目之前，我将请
我们的名誉副主席兼商务参赞
A. H. George先生向各位讲话。
随后，A. H. George先生向会议发
言，谈到了目前中国的总体贸易
状况。
经Robert Calder-Marshall爵士提
议，C. H. Arnhold先生附议，报告
和账目获通过。

stated, have made it compulsory for
all foreign steamers operating in
the lower reaches of the Yangtse
River to obtain navigation permits.

firms have refused to comply with
the measure, a large number of
their steamers have been forced to
suspend service.

the operation by foreign companies

which was reported by one of our
contemporaries provides a good case

"Japan Slams The Open Door"
Vast Foreign Investments Said
Threatened By Japan's Campaign

U. S. $3,000,000,000
Said Imperiled By
Restrictions

Japan's war on foreign interests in China today threatens to wipe out the work of four generations of foreign traders, shippers, missionaries and educators.

In cold cash, the total value of threatened foreign business and cultural investments is estimated to amount to more than US$3,000,000,000.

Much of the damage done by the Japanese fighting services and their close allies—the super-trusts of Tokyo—is already irretrievable. A considerable amount, however, may still be salvaged by quick, co-ordinated action by the powers whose interests are menaced.

In her campaign to build a vast continental empire and a "new order in Asia," Japan is following two well-defined lines of attack:

Firstly, a determined onslaught against international treaties which form the broad foundation of foreign rights and interests in this country;

Secondly, a vicious campaign of bayonet-backed restrictions on every form of foreign activity in Japanese-occupied areas.

In repudiating treaties of which she has been a solemn signatory, Japan is seeking to establish a new **〔此处转录不清〕** which aims to perpetuate her hegemony in East Asia. This new doctrine naturally and inevitably seeks to throw overboard the old, established principles of "open door" and equal opportunity for foreigners in China.

Tokyo Repudiates
Especially significant to foreign-
ers in China are Tokyo's repeated
declarations that the "changed
conditions in the Orient" have
"out-dated" the Nine-Power Pact,
which forms the corner-stone of
international relations in the
Pacific.
Tokyo's verbal attacks on the
Washington treaty have been time
and again translated into action
by the Japanese armies of invasion
in China.
By force and intimidation, for-
eigners have been excluded from
every corner of the Japanese-
overrun territory. Today, the bulk
of China's foreign population is
concentrated in isolated "islands"
in Shameen, Hankow, Tientsin,
Tsingtao and Shanghai.
Simultaneously, all of China's
waterways, including the Yangtse,
have been barred to foreign trade,
travel and shipping. Repeated
foreign protests have been either
ignored or countered with specious
pleas of "military necessity."
But while the interior has been
closed to the foreigners and for-
eign goods, the Japanese trader
and industrialist has had a free
run of the land, thus enabling
them to secure a powerful foothold
in the immensely rich China
market.

Monopolies Formed
With the expulsion of foreign
trader and merchandise, Nippon-
made goods have flooded the "oc-
cupied" areas, huge Japanese
trading firms have extended their
tentacles to every part of the
once-free market, and Army-backed
trusts have established monopolies
dominating all phases of economic
life.
That the Japanese intend to
make their stranglehold on the oc-
cupied territory permanent is
abundantly indicated. No better
proof of this is needed than
belligerent statements issued in
Tokyo, the ambitious plans for the
monopolistic exploitation of China's
resources, and, finally, the transfer
of the direction of the Japanese
activities in this country to the
Army-dominated and staffed Asia
Development Board.
Foreign interests in China face
the most critical situation in a
century. Protests, notes and repre-
sentations have thus far proved
useless. Japan's campaign of re-
pression vitally affects the interests
of every foreigner in China, whe-
ther he be a merchant, a banker
or a missionary. A clear under-
standing of the current develop-
ments is, therefore, essential.
It is to aid this understanding
that THE CHINA PRESS is pub-
lishing a series of special articles
on the general subject of "Japan
Slams The Open Door."

东京予以否认
对于在华外国人而言，尤其重要的是东京反复声明，“东方局势的变化”已使构成太平洋国际关系基石的《九国公约》“过时”。
东京对华盛顿条约的口头攻击，已一次次被侵华日军转化为实际行动。
通过武力和恐吓，外国人被排除在日本占领领土的每一个角落。如今，大部分在华外籍人口集中在沙面、汉口、天津、青岛和上海的孤立“孤岛”中。
与此同时，包括长江在内的中国所有水道都禁止了外国贸易、旅行和航运。外国的多次抗议要么被无视，要么以似是而非的“军事需要”为由加以反驳。
但是，虽然内地对外国人和外国商品关闭，日本商人和工业家却可以在这片土地上自由往来，从而使他们能够在极其富有的中国市场获得强有力的立足点。

形成垄断
随着外国商人和商品的被驱逐，日本制造的商品淹没了“占领”区，大型日本贸易公司将其触角延伸至曾经自由的市场的各个部分，而在军队支持下的托拉斯则建立了主导经济生活各个阶段的垄断。
日本意图使其对被占领领土的扼制永久化，这一点已表现得十分明显。无需比东京发布的好战声明、垄断性开发中国资源的雄心勃勃的计划，以及最终将日本在华活动的指挥权移交给由陆军主导和配备人员的兴亚院（Asia Development Board），更好的证据了。
在华外国利益面临一个世纪以来最危急的局势。迄今为止，抗议、照会和交涉均证明无效。日本的镇压运动严重影响着每一个在华外国人的利益，无论他是商人、银行家还是传教士。因此，清楚地了解当前事态发展至关重要。
为了帮助理解这一情况，《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）正在刊登一系列关于“日本抨击门户开放政策”这一总体主题的特别文章。

CHINA PRESS.
FEB 1 4 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8831
Date ____ / __ / __

“Japan Slams The Open Door”
Nippon Said Tightening Grip On
China’s Communication Channels

Japanese Said Enabled
To Transport Troops
To All Fronts

Calmly ignoring half-hearted protests of the Great Powers, the Japanese Fighting Services are today continuing to tighten their stranglehold on China’s channels of communication, in which foreign investors have a stake of more than U.S. $300,000,000.

The Japanese strategy, apparently formulated a year ago when Tokyo realized that it had a major war on its hands, was well-considered and carried out with admirable precision.

Control of the means of communication assured the Japanese of the following important advantages:

1. It enabled the Japanese Army to transport quickly its troops and mechanical equipment from one front to another;
2. It played an important role in Tokyo’s plans to “starve out” Free China, by cutting off her insulating routes and preventing the exports of goods abroad;
3. It divided China into numerous regions without contact with each other, and therefore, more amenable to Japanese political and military pressure and propaganda;
4. It kept foreigners out of the interior, thus removing one of the factors militating against Japan’s policy and ensuring the absolute control of Nippon’s hegemony over East Asia;
5. It enabled the Japanese under occupation thereof to get protection beyond fear of challenge by the foreign competitors;
6. It finally, placed in Japan’s hands a formidable “trump card” with which she can eventually force any power which is in sympathy with China to come to terms.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

（批：C 14/2）
（批：Q 14/-）

1939年2月14日

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别登记处（S. B. REGISTRY）
编号 S. B. D. 8831
日期 ____ / __ / __

“日本抨击门户开放政策”
据称日本加紧控制中国的交通通道

据称日本得以
向前线各处
运送军队

日本战斗部队冷静地无视列强半心半意的抗议，今日继续加紧扼制中国的交通通道，外国投资者在这些通道中的权益超过3亿美元。

日本的战略显然是在一年前制定的，当时东京意识到自己卷入了一场大规模战争，该战略经过深思熟虑，并以令人钦佩的精确度得以执行。

控制交通手段确保了日本获得以下重要优势：

1. 使日本军队能够迅速将其部队和机械设备从一个前线运送到另一个前线；
2. 在东京“饿死”自由中国的计划中发挥了重要作用，切断了其隔离路线并阻止货物出口到国外；
3. 将中国划分为众多彼此没有联系的区域，因此更容易受到日本政治和军事压力及宣传的影响；
4. 将外国人阻挡在内地之外，从而消除了阻碍日本政策的一个因素，并确保日本对东亚霸权的绝对控制；
5. 使在被占领土上的日本人能够获得保护，无需担心外国竞争对手的挑战；
6. 最后，使日本手中掌握了一张强大的“王牌”，凭借此牌她最终可以迫使任何同情中国的强国与其妥协。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

page_data.en:
When — and if — the Japanese
troops complete the occupation of
the entire line, they will have est-
ablished a steel ring round the
greater and richer part of China.
Japan's task then will be to clear
this enormous area of Chinese
troops and irreconcilable elements,
establish a puppet federated regime
and literally to strangle the popula-
tion into acquiescence to Nipponese
imperial plans.

In achieving this goal, Japan is
treading heavily upon foreign toes.
Foreign investors have poured im-
mense funds into the development
of China's coastal and river ship-
ping and railways. It was also
through the maintenance of free
and efficient communications that
foreign traders found access to the
vast Chinese market.

Of the funds invested in com-
munications, the bulk has apparent-
ly already been irretrievably lost.
relatively unimportant coastal ship-
ping services, a portion of the Can-
ton-Hankow Railway, the Yunnan
line, and foreign cable and radio
facilities in Shanghai—is in im-
mediate jeopardy.

Free movement Needed

The survival of foreign interests
in China depends on the ability of
the Powers to compel Japan to re-
store free access to China's chan-
nels of communication, for, direct-
ly and indirectly, foreign commerce,
industry and banking in this coun-
try will die if communications with
the interior are severed.

Seven years ago, the American
investment in transportation (avia-
tion, railways, shipping etc.) total-
led $10,799,918 out of total American
investments of $150,000,000. The
figures for the months immediately
preceding the invasion of North
China in July, 1937, were still great-
er, largely as the result of the
phenomenal development of China's
commercial aviation and radio com-
munication and broadcasting.

Comparable gains were made by
British investments, which, in 1931,
reached U.S. $134,900,000, or 14 per
cent of Britain's total stake in
China at that time of $1,189,200,-
000.

In addition to U.S. $70,000,000 re-
presenting British holdings in
Chinese Government railway and
other communications bonds, John
Bull's interest in this country's
communications was worth in the
beginning of 1937 well in excess of
$250,000,000.

The fate of these enormous in-
vestments depends solely upon the
ability of the Great Powers to com-
pel Japan to restore access to
China's channels of communication.

But the issue is even of greater
import than mere recovery of $250,-
000,000 or $300,000,000. Communica-
tions in China form the foundation
of foreign trade, industry and bank-
ing. By closing railways and water-
ways to foreigners, the Japanese
Army has already dealt a well-nigh
fatal blow to foreign commerce
(which, in the case of Britain, forms
a fourth of the total investments
in China).
page_data.zh:
当——如果——日本军队完成整条防线的占领时，他们将在中国更大、更富裕的部分周围建立一个钢铁包围圈。届时，日本的任务将是清除这一广大区域内的中国军队和不妥协分子，建立一个傀儡联邦政权，并从字面上通过窒息手段迫使民众默许日本的帝国计划。

在实现这一目标的过程中，日本严重侵犯了外国人的利益。外国投资者已将巨额资金投入中国沿海和内河航运及铁路的发展。也正是通过维持自由高效的交通，外国商人才得以进入庞大的中国市场。

在投入交通领域的资金中，大部分显然已经无法挽回地损失了。相对不重要的沿海航运服务、粤汉铁路的一部分、滇越铁路线，以及上海的外国电缆和无线电设施——正处于直接的危险之中。

需要自由通行

在华外国利益的存续取决于各强国能否迫使日本恢复对中国交通通道的自由 access，因为如果与内地的联系被切断，该国直接或间接的外国商业、工业和银行业都将消亡。

七年前，美国在交通运输业（航空、铁路、航运等）的投资总额为10,799,918美元，占美国总投资额1.5亿美元的一部分。在1937年7月入侵华北之前几个月的数字甚至更大，这在很大程度上是由于中国商业航空和无线电通信及广播事业的惊人发展。

英国投资也取得了可比的增长，1931年达到1.349亿美元，占当时英国在华总投资额11.892亿美元的14%。

除了代表英国持有中国政府铁路及其他交通债券的7,000万美元外，约翰牛（John Bull，指英国）在华交通领域的权益在1937年初价值远超2.5亿美元。

这些巨额投资的命运完全取决于各强国能否迫使日本恢复对中国交通通道的 access。

但这一问题的重要性甚至超过了仅仅收回2.5亿或3亿美元。中国的交通构成了外国贸易、工业和银行业的基础。通过禁止外国人使用铁路和水路，日本军队已经给外国商业（就英国而言，占其在华总投资的四分之一）造成了近乎致命的打击。

page_data.en:
Shipping Suffers Most

Particularly hard hit by the Japanese restrictive measures has been shipping. While a good many foreign steamship companies are reaping a golden harvest today transporting Chinese cargo and passengers through the Japanese blockade, this prosperity is short-lived.

Japanese measures, already taken and those planned, openly aim at the exclusion of foreign bottoms from the waterways of East Asia. One of the world's greatest rivers, the Yangtse, has been completely closed to non-Japanese vessels. A similar situation prevails in the waterways radiating from Shanghai and Canton.

All varieties of restrictions are also being invoked to hinder and obstruct foreign shipping along the China coast. These obstacles range from the virtual closure of important ports, such as Tsingtao, to foreign steamers to pin-prick hindrances, such as excessive zeal in the observance of quarantine regulations.

But all these restrictions are dwarfed by the scope of plans now nearing completion at the offices of the General Staff and the financial houses of Mitsui and Mitsubishi in Tokyo.

Under the provisions of this ambitious scheme, scheduled for materialization before the end of the current year, all Japanese shipping companies operating in China and between Japan and this country will be merged into a shipping octopus, whose tentacles will extend to every corner of East Asia.

The publicly-avowed aim of the Army-supported sponsors of this huge, semi-official concern is to drive foreign shipping interests, mainly British, from the Orient.

That the projected firm faced roscate prospects was indicated by the success of the so-called China Inland Navigation Company, which succeeded in establishing a monopoly on shipping in waterways radiating from Shanghai without a murmur of protest from foreign Powers despite the importance of the precedent.

Competitor Issues Passes

The Japanese Navy added a ludicrous touch to the situation by endowing the Nipponese firm with the right to issue passes for navigation in waters which it reserved for its own use.

Even more desperate, from the foreign point of view, has been the situation with railways. While there were no foreign-owned railways in China proper before the outbreak of the war, foreign investments in railway bonds and other obligations probably exceeded U.S. $125,000,000.

With the National Government making every effort to service and redeem railway loans and making ambitious plans for the development of the country's communications, the bonds gradually forged to the forefront of Chinese securities.

All this, however, was changed the moment the Japanese troops invaded China 15 months ago. Starting with the short stretch between the Great Wall and Peiping, the Nipponese Army gradually seized control of most of China's lines, from the dusty plains of Inner Mongolia to Kwangtung.
page_data.zh:
航运业受创最重

受日本限制性措施打击尤为严重的是航运业。尽管目前许多外国轮船公司通过日本封锁线运输中国货物和乘客，正赚取丰厚利润，但这种繁荣是短暂的。

日本已采取及计划中的措施，公然旨在将外国船只排除在东亚水道之外。世界最大河流之一的长江，已完全禁止非日本船只通行。以上海和广州为中心辐射的水道也盛行着类似的情况。

各种各样的限制措施也被用来阻碍和妨碍沿中国海岸的外国航运。这些障碍范围广泛，从实际上向外国轮船关闭青岛等重要港口，到诸如在执行检疫规定时过度热心这类琐碎的阻挠。

但是，与东京参谋本部办公室以及三井和三菱财团中即将完成的计划规模相比，所有这些限制都显得微不足道。

根据这项雄心勃勃的计划条款——预计在今年年底前实现——所有在中国运营以及在日本与中国之间运营的日本航运公司将合并为一个航运垄断巨头，其触角将延伸至东亚的每一个角落。

这一庞大的半官方企业的发起者得到陆军支持，他们公开宣称的目标是将外国（主要是英国）航运利益逐出东方。

所谓的“中华内河航运公司”的成功表明，这家拟议中的公司面临着广阔的前景；尽管先例意义重大，但该公司成功地在以上海为中心辐射的水道上建立了航运垄断，而未引起外国列强的任何抗议。

竞争对手签发通行证

日本海军为局势增添了一抹荒诞色彩，它赋予这家日本公司在为其自身保留的水域中签发航行通行证的权利。

从外国人的角度来看，铁路方面的情况更为严峻。虽然在中国本土（China proper），战前没有外资拥有的铁路，但外国在铁路债券和其他债务上的投资可能超过了1.25亿美元。

随着国民政府竭尽全力偿还和赎回铁路贷款，并为国家交通发展制定宏伟计划，这些债券逐渐成为中国证券中的佼佼者。

然而，这一切在15个月前日军入侵中国的那一刻发生了改变。从长城与北平之间的短短一段铁路开始，日军逐渐控制了从中国内蒙古的尘土飞扬的平原到广东的大部分铁路线。

page_data.en:
As soon as the railways were
repaired by Army engineers, their
management was entrusted to the
South Manchuria Railway Com-
pany, Dai Nippon's "East Indies
Company" and Asia's greatest con-
cern. Working hand in glove with
the military, the S.M.R. Im-
mediately barred foreign access to
the railway facilities and terminat-
ed the servicing of bonds secured
on revenues of these lines.
Even more drastic were the
means employed by the Japanese
Navy to put an end to the activi-
ties of China's two Sino-foreign
aviation companies,—the Sino-
American China National Aviation
Corporation and the Sino-German
Eurasia Aviation Corporation.
Japanese pursuit planes simply
chased passenger air liners of the
two concerns and machine-gunned
them. It was later easy to plead
that the Japanese fliers had mis-
taken the clearly distinguishable
Douglas and Junker passenger
craft for Chinese bombers.
**Japanese Air Lines Opened**
The attacks on planes partly
owned by foreign interests were
accompanied by the inauguration
of air lines linking Tokyo, Fukuoka
and Dairen with the major cities
in the Japanese-occupied territory
in China. Only a week after the
fall of Hankow, passenger machines
were leaving the city tri-weekly
for the airports of Nippon.
This, incidentally, was one of the
most striking illustrations of the
meaning of Japan's solemnly re-
iterated pledges to respect the
principles of "Open Door" and
"Equal Opportunity" in China.
Simultaneously with the seizure
of railways and the closure of
China's waterways to foreign ship-
ping, the Japanese Army took over
all facilities for the communica-
tion of the written and spoken
word. While legally speaking Japan
had merely taken over the services
once operated by the Chinese Gov-
ernment, there was a vital differ-
ence from the foreign point of
view.
Before the war, a foreign trader
could send a message by tele-
graph, radio or telephone to any
part of the country with the as-
surance that it would reach the
addressee in the form in which it
was originally drafted. The Japan-
ese Army altered this orthodox
procedure.
Most of the Japanese-occupied
area was completely closed to non-
Nipponese messages on the vague
grounds of "military necessity."
The restrictions, however, did not
apply to Japanese traders. Where
messages were allowed to be sent,
they were as often as not delibera-
tely garbled or censored beyond
recognition.
**Messages Rewritten**
Similar treatment was accorded
to foreign press messages, the
Japanese military censors even
going to the extent of rewriting
parts of messages to suit the ends
of propaganda. Numerous protests,
notably in Peiping and Tientsin
where the censors were especially
exuberant, failed either to elicit
replies from Tokyo or to bring
about an amelioration of condi-
tions.
page_data.zh:
铁路一经陆军工程师修复，其管理权便移交给了南满洲铁道株式会社（South Manchuria Railway Company），即大日本的“东印度公司”和亚洲最大的企业。南满铁道株式会社与军方紧密勾结，立即禁止外国人使用铁路设施，并终止了以这些线路收入为担保的债券的服务。

日本海军为终结中国两家中外合资航空公司的活动所采取的手段更为激烈——这两家公司分别是中美合资的中国航空公司（China National Aviation Corporation）和中德合资的欧亚航空公司（Eurasia Aviation Corporation）。日本战斗机直接追逐这两家公司的客运航班并用机枪扫射。事后，日方飞行员轻易地辩称，他们将清晰可辨的道格拉斯（Douglas）和容克（Junker）客机误认为中国轰炸机。

**日本航线开通**

对外资部分拥有的飞机发动的攻击，伴随着连接东京、福冈和大连与中国日占区主要城市的航线的开通而进行。汉口沦陷仅一周后，客机便每周三次从该市起飞，前往日本的机场。

顺便提一下，这是对日本一再庄严承诺尊重在华“门户开放”和“机会均等”原则之含义的最引人注目的诠释之一。

在夺取铁路和对外国航运关闭中国水道的同时，日本陆军接管了所有书面和口头通讯设施。虽然从法律上讲，日本只是接管了曾由中国政府运营的服务，但从外国人的角度来看，存在至关重要的差异。

战前，外国商人可以通过电报、无线电或电话向全国任何地方发送信息，并确信信息将以最初起草的形式送达收件人。日本陆军改变了这一常规程序。

出于模糊的“军事需要”理由，大部分日占区完全禁止非日本人发送信息。然而，这些限制并不适用于日本商人。在允许发送信息的地方，信息往往被故意篡改或审查得面目全非。

**信息被重写**

外国新闻电讯也受到了类似的对待，日本军事检查员甚至到了为了宣传目的而重写部分电讯内容的地步。无数抗议，特别是在检查员尤其猖獗的北平和天津，既未能引来东京的回复，也未能改善状况。

page_data.en:
As in shipping, the Japanese
were not content to enjoy a posi-
tion of dominance. Special tele-
phone and telegraph concerns were
established under the North and
Central China Development Com-
panies to monopolize the business.
Especially hard hit by this move
were American and German in-
terests, which have been doing a
thriving trade in telephone and
radio equipment before the war.
Parallel to the censorship of
wire and wireless messages went
the censorship of mails and the
press. Operating under the shroud
of secrecy, Japanese censors have
been playing havoc with foreign
mails in the major ports. Numer-
ous protests have remained un-
answered.
Of Japan's illegal actions in
China, her drive to seize complete
control of communications must
be watched with especial appre-
hension, for it is by these means
that the Japanese Army intends to
expel foreign interests from China
and to secure Chinese acquiescence
to the Nipponese imperial plans.
If foreign Powers are to take
action to protect their imperilled
interests here, such action must
first come in the field of com-
munications. And the projected
establishment of a shipping mono-
poly presents an opportunity for
a determined foreign move.
page_data.zh:
与航运业一样，日本人并不满足于占据主导地位。在华北开发会社和华兴公司（Central China Development Companies）下成立了专门的电话和电报公司，以垄断该业务。受此举措打击尤为严重的是美国和德国的利益，它们在战前曾在电话和无线电设备贸易中大获成功。

与对有线和无线信息的审查并行的是对邮件和新闻界的审查。日本检查员在秘密掩护下运作，一直在主要港口严重破坏外国邮件。无数抗议仍未得到答复。

在日本在华的非法行动中，其夺取通讯完全控制权的企图必须受到特别警惕，因为日本陆军打算通过这些手段将外国利益逐出中国，并确保中国人对日本帝国计划的默许。

如果外国列强要采取行动保护其在华岌岌可危的利益，这种行动必须首先出现在通讯领域。而拟议建立的航运垄断则为外国采取坚决行动提供了一个机会。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
FEB 10 1939
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. I. REGISTRY
No. S. A. D.

“Japan Slams The Open Door”
Hostile Attitude Towards Foreign
Traders In China Is Said Mounting
Protests Of Britain,
U.S., France Go
Unanswered

Backing solidly for the first time
since the outbreak of hostilities the
interests of foreign traders in
China, the British, French and
American Governments in mid-
January delivered notes to Japan,
demanding in the strongest terms
the maintenance of the Open Door
principle. The notes were parallel
and requested an early reply, which
a month since their delivery has
not yet been forthcoming.

In the meantime, a survey of the
situation reveals, a strengthening of
Japan's hostile attitude, both offi-
cially and unofficially, directly and
indirectly, towards foreign traders
has been witnessed, and although
the most insistent demands have
been made through diplomatic
channels for the immediate cessa-
tion of incidents involving foreign
nationals, no attempt appears to
have been made to satisfy the de-
mands.

Since the delivery of the three
notes alone, the position has turn-
ed for the worse, and latest de-
velopment in what has all the ear-
marks of a planned campaign of
interference with foreign rights in
China has been the seizure and
detention of three steamships, one
British and two Norwegian, on the
flimsy pretext of "suspicion," fol-
lowed immediately by the subse-
quent detention of two more Bri-
tish steamers in Chefoo.

Unjustified Action

On none of these occasions could
the Japanese authorities justify
their action, and in the Chefoo
case, circumstances were such as to
give rise to the grave suspicion
that the vessels were deliberately
detained in order to permit a com-
peting Japanese-owned line es-
tablish a swifter schedule.

Details of the detention of the
Jardine steamers Taisang and
Wingsang, the two vessels concern-
ed must still be fresh in the pub-
lic mind, and in view of the fact
that the antecedents of the two
vessels had been highly publicized,
the excuse of the Japanese authori-
ties that they wished to investigate
the "status of the ships" cannot be
accepted.

Further, since the dispatch of the
notes to Tokyo, there has been a
new outbreak of petty interference
with foreign freedom of movement
in various occupied cities and ports,
such as the order that all foreign-
ers must be equipped with passes
in Tientsin, Chefoo and Tsingtao.

《字林西报》
1939年2月10日
上海公共租界工部局
S. I. 登记处
编号 S. A. D.

“日本关上大门”
据称对华外商敌视态度加剧
英、美、法抗议未获回应

自敌对行动爆发以来，英国、法国和美国政府首次在月中旬发出照会，坚定支持在华外国商人的利益，以最强烈的措辞要求维持“门户开放”原则。这些照会内容平行，并要求尽早回复，但在发出一个月后，至今尚未收到回复。

与此同时，对局势的调查显示，日本官方和非官方、直接和间接地对外国商人的敌视态度正在加强，尽管已通过外交渠道提出最迫切的要求，要求立即停止涉及外国国民的事件，但似乎并未做出任何努力来满足这些要求。

自三份照会发出以来，局势进一步恶化，而在这一具有精心策划的干涉在华外国权利战役特征的事件中，最新的发展是以“嫌疑”为薄弱借口扣押并拘留了三艘轮船（一艘英国籍，两艘挪威籍），随后又在烟台拘留了两艘英国轮船。

无理行动

在这些事件中，日本当局均无法为其行为提供正当理由，而在烟台一案中，情况使人严重怀疑这些船只被故意扣留，以便让一家竞争性的日本所属轮船公司建立更快的船期。

怡和洋行（Jardine）轮船“泰山”号（Taisang）和“永山”号（Wingsang）被拘留的细节，公众想必仍记忆犹新；鉴于这两艘船的背景已被广泛公开报道，日本当局声称希望调查“船舶身份”的借口是不能接受的。

此外，自向东京发出照会以来，在各个被占领的城市和港口，对外国人行动自由的小规模干涉再次爆发，例如命令在天津、烟台和青岛的所有外国人必须持有通行证。

page_data.en:
Export Restrictions

More serious still, the long-ex-
pected extension of export permit
restrictions, by which all export
bills must be cleared through the
Yokohama Specie Bank, has reach-
ed Chefoo, and although a respite
has been granted by the Japanese
authorities to February 15, it has
been emphasized that the restric-
tion remains in force.
The gravity with which America,
Great Britain and France regard
the accumulated evidence of Jap-
anese encroachment on foreign
rights is clearly reflected in Lon-
don's note, the first of the three
communications to be delivered to
Tokyo.
After recalling the statements of
Prince Konoye, then Prime Minister
of Japan, on November 3 and
December 22, and Mr. Hachiro
Arita's press statement on Decem-
ber 19, the note said that the un-
certainty and grave concern arous-
ed over these two pronouncements
had not been removed by the con-
versations between Sir Robert
Craigie and Mr. Arita. The note
further refused to accept Japan's
definition of the "new order in
Asia."

Anti-Foreign Measures

International expert opinion has
agreed here and abroad that the
main line of Japan's attitude to-
wards foreign trading interests in
China is indicated by the follow-
ing restrictive actions enforced by
the Japanese authorities wherever
and whenever territory has come
under their control:
1. Closure to all merchants ex-
cept Japanese nationals, of all trade
routes, railways and inland water-
ways;
2. Discriminatory exchange con-
trol operating directly or indirectly
against foreign traders;
3. Granting of monopoly condi-
tions to Japanese traders, to the
exclusion of foreign merchants;
4. Restrictive measures against
freedom of foreign movement in oc-
cupied areas;
5. Imposition of totally illegal
censorship of foreign letters, parcels
and telegrams;
6. Interference with the normal
collection of revenue by the Cus-
toms, and enforcement of a tariff
rate which is alleged to have dis-
criminated against foreign trade.
There are numerous other more
or less petty restrictions enforced
by the Japanese authorities, but
outside of these six outstanding
measures, the closure of the north-
ern and eastern districts of Shang-
hai has drawn the strongest con-
demnation and the most vigorous
protests from the various foreign
governments, and particularly the
British Government.
page_data.zh:
出口限制

更为严重的是，备受期待的出口许可证限制的扩展——据此所有出口账单必须通过横滨正金银行清算——已延伸至烟台，尽管日本当局给予宽限至2月15日，但强调该限制仍然有效。

美国、英国和法国对日本侵蚀外国权利的累积证据的重视程度，清楚地反映在伦敦的照会中，这是递交给东京的三份文件中的第一份。

照会在回顾时任日本首相近卫文麿亲王于11月3日和12月22日的声明，以及有田八郎先生于12月19日的新闻声明后指出，克莱琪爵士（Sir Robert Craigie）与有田先生之间的会谈并未消除人们对这两项声明所产生的不确定性和严重关切。照会进一步拒绝接受日本对“亚洲新秩序”的定义。

排外措施

国内外的国际专家意见一致认为，日本对华外国贸易利益态度的主线，体现在日本当局在其控制领土的任何地方和任何时候执行的以下限制性行动中：
1. 除日本国民外，对所有商人关闭所有贸易路线、铁路和内河水道；
2. 实施直接或间接针对外国商人的歧视性外汇管制；
3. 授予日本商人垄断地位，排斥外国商人；
4. 对被占领地区外国人行动自由的限制措施；
5. 对外国信件、包裹和电报实施完全非法的审查；
6. 干扰海关正常征收税款，并强制执行据称歧视外国贸易的关税税率。

日本当局还实施了许多其他或多或少的琐碎限制，但除了这六项突出措施外，上海北部和东部地区的封闭引起了各外国政府，特别是英国政府的最强烈谴责和最有力抗议。

page_data.en:
“Blockade” Of Shanghai
No part of China's economic struc-
ture has escaped completely the
disastrous effects of more than a
year of hostilities waged within the
nation by Japan, but it has been
the virtual blockade of Shanghai,
the country's trade nerve-center,
that has had the most paralyzing
effect on commerce and industry.
That is the considered opinion of
both Chinese and foreign financiers
and merchants not only in Shang-
hai, but in other parts of China as
well.
Practically every restrictive action
taken by the Japanese against for-
eign trade interests, it has been
pointed out by one of Shanghai's
leading British traders, hinged on
Japan's power to close Shanghai's
vital overland outlets—even the clo-
sure of the Yangtse would have been
rendered ineffectual had these trade
routes been left open to operate.
Shanghai's position as a financial
center has been attacked again and
again by currency manipulation
and exchange restrictions in Japan-
ese occupied territory, and although
most of those measures have fail-
ed, it has been shown that the
isolation of Shanghai from the in-
terior might easily have had a
damaging effect on the whole of
the country's currency.
“Base Of Invasion”
The British trader referred to
above, declared in an interview with
THE CHINA PRESS that the Japan-
ese economic attack on Shanghai
could not have been more deli-
berate, nor more intense, had the
international port been the objec-
tive of Japan's invasion, instead of
its base. “Everything possible has
been done by the Japanese govern-
ment-backed interests to reduce
foreign interests in Shanghai to
economic ruin,” he continued.
“Whether it is the closure of the
northern and eastern districts, con-
taining millions upon millions of
dollars worth of foreign invest-
ments and property, the prohibi-
tion of foreign movement in the
occupied zones, the closure of the
Yangtse River, or any of the many
other measures taken, there can be
discerned clearly in them the ob-
vious Japanese intention to make
of China a second Manchuria.”
The past was gone and irretriev-
able, along with vanished trade
and property, he continued, and
foreign interests were now looking
forward with alarm to a future as
gloomy as it could be, with the
only ray of hope the growing pres-
sure being applied by the Powers
against Japanese monopolistic acti-
vities. And unless this pressure
was increased swiftly, he added, the
position would become so desperate
that a complete flight of confidence
would have the effect desired by the
Japanese—that of driving foreign
trade out of China.
page_data.zh:
上海的“封锁”

中国任何一部分的经济结构都未能完全逃脱日本在国内进行的一年多敌对行动所带来的灾难性影响，但对该国贸易神经中枢上海的实际封锁，已对工商业产生了最为瘫痪性的影响。这不仅是上海，而且是中国其他地区的中西金融家和商人经过深思熟虑后的共同看法。

上海一位主要的英国贸易商指出，日本针对外国贸易利益所采取的几乎每一项限制性行动，都取决于日本关闭上海至关重要的陆路出口的能力——即使这些贸易路线保持开放，长江的封锁本也会变得无效。

上海作为金融中心的地位一再受到日占区货币操纵和外汇限制的冲击，虽然大多数此类措施均已失败，但这表明，上海与内地的隔绝很容易会对整个国家的货币体系产生破坏性影响。

“入侵基地”

上述那位英国贸易商在接受《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS）采访时宣称，如果这个国际港口是日本入侵的目标而非其基地的话，日本对上海的经济攻击也不可能更加蓄意或更加猛烈。“在日本政府支持的势力努力下，一切可能的手段都被用来使上海的外国利益陷入经济崩溃，”他继续说道。“无论是封闭拥有价值数以百万计美元的外国投资和财产的北部和东部地区，禁止外国人在占领区活动，封锁长江，还是采取其他许多措施，从中都可以清楚地看出日本明显的意图，即把中国变成第二个满洲。”

他继续说，过去已一去不复返，随着贸易和财产的消失，外国利益现在正惊恐地展望着一个尽可能阴暗的未来，唯一的希望之光在于列强对日本垄断活动施加的压力日益增大。他补充说，除非迅速增加这种压力，否则局势将变得如此绝望，以至于信心的完全丧失将产生日本所期望的效果——即将外国贸易赶出中国。

page_data.en:
Confidence Needed
Restoration of confidence in
Shanghai, he said, was the primary
necessity of today, and that could
only be attained by a restoration of
the Settlement north of Soochow
Creek to the rightful authorities,
the re-opening of occupied zones
within reasonable limits, and the
return of the railways to the ad-
ministrations.
Once those steps had been taken,
the merchant continued, he had
little doubt that the restoration of
normality in the interior would be
achieved speedily and without fur-
ther loss of trade.
It had to be regretted, he de-
clared, that there appeared to be
so little understanding in England
and other countries of the true
position in China so far as foreign
trade was concerned. It was a
position which needed more than
the academic exchange of diplo-
matic notes and protests and
apologies ad nauseam; it was be-
coming increasingly clear that the
western powers would have to re-
sort the weapon of retaliation,
which applied firmly and justly,
would undoubtedly have far more
effect than all the efforts of the
foreign offices have had to date.
America's Losses
Reviewing briefly the development
of Japanese control over trade in
North and Central China, a lead-
ing American business man in
Shanghai was no less emphatic.
Quoting figures announced by Mr.
Julean Arnold, American Commer-
cial Attache in Shanghai, he ob-
served that American trade in
China has so far suffered to the
extent of $200,000,000.
Mr. Arnold declared in his address
that the dogma that American trade
with Japan was far more valuable
than that with China was a
"delusion." While they were having
an immediate gain in Japanese
trade through the sale of war ma-
terials, that would be cancelled by
appalling losses in Chinese trade in
the future should China lose.
"When hostilities began in July,
1937," declared Mr. Arnold "China
presented to the world the most
alluring picture in prospects of in-
creased trade. China, with a quarter
of the world's population was em-
barking on a vast modernization
program which would have startled
the world. We were favored with
prospects for the annual sale to
China of hundreds of millions of
dollars worth of peace time com-
modities. Now our cotton and to-
bacco markets in Japan will be wiped
out if China falls, for China will be
reduced to a condition of serfdom and
obliged to grow not only all the
cotton needed for Japan's vast
textile industries, but also the
tobacco for her government tobacco
monopoly."
Two-Fold Loss
Mr. Arnold pointed out what he
declared was already a two-fold
loss in commerce with China, suf-
fered by America through Japan-
ese war measures and forecast even
greater losses if the Nipponese
armies are victorious.
"After the Japanese marched
their armies into Manchuria we
were assured that the 'open door'
policy would be restored," he said.
"Judging by what has happened to
our trade in those areas, we must
conclude that this Japanese open-
door is a two-fold affair. Upon one
fold is the word 'in'. It is reserved
for the Japanese. On the other
fold is the word 'out.' This is in-
tended for all others."
page_data.zh:
需要信心

他说，恢复对上海的信心是当今的首要需求，而这只有通过将苏州河以北的租界交还给合法当局、在合理范围内重新开放占领区以及将铁路归还给管理部门才能实现。

这位商人继续说，一旦采取这些步骤，他毫不怀疑内地的正常状态将迅速恢复，且不会造成进一步的贸易损失。

他宣称，令人遗憾的是，英国和其他国家似乎对中国在外贸方面的真实处境缺乏了解。这种局面需要的不仅仅是外交照会、抗议和没完没了的道歉这类学术性的交换；越来越清楚的是，西方列强将不得不诉诸报复武器，如果坚定而公正地加以应用，其效果无疑将远超各国外交部迄今为止的所有努力。

美国的损失

上海一位主要的美国商人在简要回顾日本对华中和华北贸易控制的发展时，态度同样坚决。他引用美国驻上海商务参赞朱利安·阿诺德（Julean Arnold）先生公布的数据指出，美国对华贸易迄今遭受的损失已达2亿美元。

阿诺德先生在演讲中宣称，认为美日贸易远比美中贸易有价值的教条是一种“错觉”。虽然他们通过出售战争物资在对日贸易中获得了即时收益，但如果中国沦陷，未来在华贸易的惊人损失将抵消这些收益。

阿诺德先生宣称：“当1937年7月敌对行动开始时，中国向世界展示了贸易增长前景中最诱人的图景。拥有世界四分之一人口的中国正着手实施一项庞大的现代化计划，这将令世界震惊。我们曾有望每年向中国销售价值数亿美元的和平时期商品。现在，如果中国沦陷，我们在日本的棉花和烟草市场将被抹去，因为中国将沦为附庸，不仅被迫种植日本庞大纺织工业所需的全部棉花，还要为其政府烟草专卖局种植烟草。”

双重损失

阿诺德先生指出了他所称的美国在与华商业中已经遭受的双重损失，这是由日本的战争措施造成的，并预测如果日军获胜，损失将更加巨大。

他说：“在日本军队开进满洲后，我们曾得到保证，‘门户开放’政策将会恢复。根据我们在那些地区的贸易遭遇来判断，我们必须得出结论，日本的这种‘门户开放’是双重的。一面写着‘进’，专供日本人使用；另一面写着‘出’，意在针对所有其他人。”

page_data.en:
Tremendous List
To itemize the proven instances
in which American and other for-
eign interests have suffered through
Japanese restrictive activities is a
task which doubtless has already
been undertaken by the various
responsible authorities, but since
these instances range from petty
fraud to bare-faced flouting of
treaty rights by huge-scale con-
cerns, a complete count here would
be impracticable.
Some indication as to the scope
of Japanese official and semi-offi-
cial violation of third-power rights,
and particularly American rights,
however, was given in the frankly-
worded document despatched on
October by Mr. Cordell Hull to
Tokyo on behalf of the United
States Government. Three demands
were made in the Note, and it may
be assumed that the demands were
made to right the wrongs imposed
by Japan. They were:
1. The discontinuance of dis-
criminatory exchange control and
of other measures imposed in areas
in China under Japanese controls
which operate either directly or in-
directly to discriminate against
American trade and enterprise;
2. The discontinuance of any
monopoly or of any preference
which would deprive American na-
tionals of the right of undertaking
any legitimate trade or industry in
China or of any arrangement which
might purport to establish in favor
of Japanese interests any general
superiority of rights with regard to
commercial or economic develop-
ment in any region of China; and
3. The discontinuance of inter-
ference by Japanese authorities in
China with American property and
other rights, including such forms
of interference as censorship of
American mail and telegrams and
restrictions upon residence and
travel by Americans and upon Amer-
ican trade and shipping.
Currency Control
Taking each of these demands in
order (and each is directly con-
nected with the others), it is
evident that the American Gov-
ernment no less than the unfor-
tunate foreign merchants in China,
sees in attempted currency control
the gravest threat to free trade.
While it must be observed that
some of the financial acrobatics
tried out by Japan have resulted in
utter failure, and the discomfiture
of their originators, even despite all
protests, there is at present no sign
that Japan will abandon her
economic attack on foreign trade.
One concrete instance of the
blunders which have been per-
petrated by the Japanese bankers
is the "National Federal Reserve
Bank," set up in North China pur-
portedly to take the place of the
"Big Four" Chinese banks. Unlike
the currency issued by the "Big
Four," however, the "Federal Re-
serve Bank" had nothing more
back its note issue than an ex-
tremely doubtful verbal promise.
Fly In The Ointment
Operating through the military,
however, the Japanese Government
immediately set about correcting
the position through the simple
process of seizing national cur-
rency found on Chinese and
giving them "Federal Reserve" cur-
rency in exchange. The idea, no
doubt was sound enough in itself as
the puppet concern soon had enough
national currency on its hands to
back its own issue.
There was soon discovered, how-
ever, a fly in the ointment which was
meant to grease the hinges of the
closing door, and not even the in-
jection of an exchange control sys-
tem was able to help the authori-
ties.
page_data.zh:
长长的清单

要逐项列出美国及其他外国利益因日本限制性活动而遭受损害的确凿实例，这无疑已是各有关主管当局正在进行的工作，但由于这些实例 ranging from  petty fraud to bare-faced flouting of treaty rights by huge-scale concerns（从小型欺诈到大型企业对条约权利的公然蔑视），在此进行完整统计是不切实际的。

然而，关于日本官方及半官方侵犯第三国权利、特别是美国权利的范围，科德尔·赫尔（Cordell Hull）先生代表美国政府于十月向东京发送的一份措辞坦率的文件中给出了一些迹象。该照会提出了三项要求，可以假定这些要求旨在纠正日本造成的不公。它们是：

1. 停止在日本控制下的中国地区实施歧视性的外汇管制及其他直接或间接歧视美国贸易和企业的措施；

2. 停止任何剥夺美国国民在中国从事任何合法贸易或工业权利的垄断或优惠，或任何旨在确立日本利益在中国任何地区商业或经济发展方面享有普遍优越权的安排；以及

3. 停止日本当局在中国对美国财产及其他权利的干涉，包括审查美国邮件和电报、限制美国人的居住和旅行以及限制美国贸易和航运等形式的干涉。

货币管制

依次审视这些要求（每一项都与其他项直接相关），显而易见，美国政府与中国不幸的外国商人一样，认为试图进行的货币管制是对自由贸易最严重的威胁。

虽然必须指出，日本尝试的一些金融花招已导致彻底失败，并使其始作俑者陷入窘境，但尽管有一切抗议，目前尚无迹象表明日本将放弃对外国贸易的经济攻击。

日本银行家所犯错误的一个具体实例是在华北设立的“国家联邦储备银行”，据称旨在取代中国“四大行”。然而，与“四大行”发行的货币不同，“联邦储备银行”的纸币发行除了极其可疑的口头承诺外，没有任何其他支撑。

瑕疵

然而，日本政府通过军方立即着手通过简单的过程来纠正这一局面：没收中国人手中的法币，并以“联邦储备”货币进行兑换。毫无疑问，这个想法本身是合理的，因为这家傀儡机构很快手中就有了足够的法币来支撑其自身的发行。

然而，人们很快发现，在这个旨在润滑即将关闭的大门的铰链的计划中存在一个瑕疵，即使是注入一套外汇管制体系也未能帮助当局解决问题。

page_data.en:
Having acquired the national currency necessary to back its note issue, the "Federal Reserve" bank was left facing the fact that the backing was good only so long as Chinese national currency was maintained at par—a discovery which Japanese merchants dumping goods in Shanghai also were to make. Result was that Japanese financiers were compelled to reverse their previous policy and deal openly in national currency.

The recently announced decision to enforce the acceptance of "military notes" also may be assumed to be a further attempt at currency control, but for the same reason that the "Federal Reserve Bank" failed, so will the "military note" scheme fail. Even in a conquered land, Japan has yet to learn, currency issues are valueless unless they are backed by metal or trade reserves, and Japan has little of either to spare.

**Exchange Manipulation**

Exchange control in Japanese occupied territory, where foreign merchants are compelled to deal through Japanese banks, and accept Yen at Tokyo quotations (far above those existing in the open market) have been the most effective weapon wielded by Japanese monopolists, for the conditions imposed have made it virtually impossible for foreign firms to deal in North China. It is anticipated that the restrictions current in North China will be extended shortly to all areas under Japanese occupation.

Although it has been alleged by the Japanese authorities that the acceptance by foreign concerns of the new customs tariff announced by the puppet regime at Peiping constituted *de facto* recognition by foreign Governments of the puppets' right to control the customs, the American Government has rightly pointed out that the assumption is arbitrary and illegal.

The new tariff nevertheless is in operation, and comes as yet another blow to foreign trade, both directly and indirectly. Loans secured on customs revenue have become a risk on the market, rather than an asset.

**Monopolies Sought**

In spite of the continued assurances of the Japanese Government that the open door of China trade will remain open under Japanese sponsored regimes, two huge holding companies were formed last year in Japan, partly financed by the Japanese Government, and for the expressly announced purpose of operating monopolies in north and central China.

The scope of enterprises in which it was announced the two companies would be interested is tremendous, ranging from complete control of communication systems, public utilities and transport, to the financing of commercial trading firms. If the Japanese Government has been sincere in its announced adherence to the open door policy, then it can only be assumed that the formation of the two companies is the most colossal fraud in the history of finance and that the companies have been floated on empty promises.

Finally, and the subject has been sufficiently well aired for the public to be fully aware of the facts, particularly in Shanghai, the restrictions imposed by the Japanese military authorities on free movement of foreigners have closed thousands of markets to all but Japanese nationals.

“联邦储备”银行在 acquiring 了支撑其纸币发行所需的法币后，不得不面对这样一个事实：这种支撑只有在维持中国法币平价的情况下才有效——这一发现，那些在上海倾销商品的日本商人也同样得出了。结果是，日本金融家被迫扭转先前的政策，公开进行法币交易。

最近宣布的强制接受“军票”的决定，也可被视为进一步控制货币的尝试，但出于与“联邦储备银行”失败相同的原因，“军票”计划也将失败。即使在被征服的土地上，日本尚未认识到，除非有金属或贸易储备作为支撑，否则发行的货币毫无价值，而日本在这两方面都几乎没有余力可资利用。

**外汇操纵**

在日本占领区，外国商人被迫通过日本银行进行交易，并按东京报价（远高于公开市场存在的汇率）接受日元，这种外汇管制已成为日本垄断主义者 wielded 的最有效武器，因为所施加的条件使得外国公司在华北开展业务 virtually 不可能。预计目前在华北实施的限制不久将扩展到所有日本占领区。

尽管日本当局声称，外国企业接受北平傀儡政权宣布的新关税税率构成了外国政府 *de facto* 承认傀儡政权拥有海关控制权，但美国政府正确地指出，这种假设是武断且非法的。

尽管如此，新关税已在实施，这对外国贸易构成了又一重打击，无论是直接还是间接。以关税收入为担保的贷款在市场上已变成一种风险，而非资产。

**谋求垄断**

尽管日本政府持续保证，在日本扶植的政权下，中国贸易的门户仍将保持开放，但去年日本成立了两大控股公司，部分资金由日本政府提供，其明确宣布的目的就是在华北和华中经营垄断事业。

据宣布，这两家公司感兴趣的企业范围极其广泛，从完全控制通信系统、公用事业和运输，到为商业贸易公司提供融资。如果日本政府对其宣布的坚持门户开放政策是真诚的，那么只能认为这两家公司的成立是金融史上最大的欺诈，这些公司是建立在空头承诺之上的。

最后，这个问题已经充分公开，公众尤其是上海公众已完全了解事实真相，日本军事当局对外国人自由流动施加的限制，已将成千上万的市场对除日本国民以外的所有人关闭。

page_data.en:
Many Restrictions
The closure of the Yangtse,
seizure of railways, closure of roads,
inland streams and waterways, and
several other restrictive actions
which cannot be excused on the
grounds of military necessity are
among the measures which have
been taken by Japanese interests
to secure what may be regarded as
monopoly rights in the occupied
zones.
It is a well-known fact that
Japanese merchants are operating
freely in river ports, that Japanese
merchant steamers are plying the
"dangerous" Yangtse, that the
Shanghai-Nanking railway is car-
rying civilian merchandise. For-
eign traders, however, are not
permitted to enter Nanking—nor
in fact any of the occupied
territory.
Taking into consideration the
known facts, the only conclusion
reached by foreign merchants is
that Japan intends to follow the
example set in "Manchukuo" so
far as foreign trade is concerned,
and that unless a determined
stand is made by Great Britain
and America on the matter, the
hard-won reward of years of for-
eign struggle and enterprise in
China must go by the board.
C-In-C's Edict
What few doubts were left in
foreign minds as to Japanese in-
tentions regarding the Yangtse
were completely dispelled by what
appears to be the final say of
Japan's army and navy, voiced
recently through their Com-
mander-In-Chief, Vice - Admiral
Oikawa, to the effect that while
hostilities last, the great river re-
mains closed to foreign traffic.
Vice-Admiral Nomura, chief of
the Japanese Special Service Sec-
tion, delivered his C-In-C's dictum
to a press conference in the follow-
ing comments:
"In view of the fact that since
the fall of the Wuhan area, the
question of the reopening of the
Yangtse River to general trade has
become the subject of discussions
by third Powers, we believe it may
not be useless to express the views
of the Japanese Forces operating in
the Yangtse area about the matter.
"It should be first noted that the
present conditions on the Yangtse
River are quite different from
those before the commencement of
hostilities. The Chinese sank or
floated thousands of mines along
the River, laid booms at Kiangyin,
Wulungshan, Matouchen, Shih-
lweiyao and Tuanfeng, and also
built strong defenses to protect
them. The Japanese forces opened
the River to their own navigation
by their up-stream operations,
overcoming the tenacious resist-
ance of the Chinese forces at a
great sacrifice.
"Great Sacrifice"
"Suppose the Japanese forces
had continued their operations
without breaking the booms set
up by the Chinese. No third Power
would be in a position to attempt
navigation on the Yangtse, at
least during the hostilities.
"The Japanese forces opened the
Yangtse in order to execute their
operations. We believe that the
third Powers who did not take
effective steps to check the block-
ading of the river, when that was
carried out by the Chinese forces
for their hostile purposes, must
now be able to realize the fact
that the Japanese forces completed
at a great sacrifice the opening of
the river solely for their military
purposes.
page_data.zh:
**诸多限制**
长江的封闭、
铁路的占领、道路、
内河溪流和水道的封闭，以及
其他几项无法以
军事必要性为由辩解的限制性行动，
是日本势力为获取在占领区
可被视为垄断权的措施中的一部分。
众所周知的事实是，
日本商人在沿江港口自由经营，
日本商船在“危险的”长江上航行，
沪宁铁路正在运送
民用货物。然而，
外国商人不被允许进入南京——事实上
也不被允许进入任何占领
领土。
考虑到已知事实，
外国商人得出的唯一结论是，
就对外贸易而言，日本打算效仿
在“满洲国”树立的先例，
除非英国和美国在此事上采取
坚定立场，否则外国人在华多年
奋斗和创业所获得的来之不易的成果
必将付诸东流。
**总司令的命令**
外国人心目中关于日本对长江
意图的仅存疑虑，已被日本陆海军
最高指挥官大川副海军上将
近期发表的看似最终定论的言论
彻底消除，其大意是：只要敌对行动
持续，这条大河就对外国交通
保持封闭。
日本特务机关长野村中将
在记者招待会上发表了以下评论，
传达了其总司令的旨意：
“鉴于武汉地区陷落后，
向一般贸易重新开放长江的问题
已成为第三国讨论的主题，
我们认为，表达在长江地区作战
的日本军队对此事的看法，
或许并非无用。
“首先应当指出，长江目前的
状况与敌对行动开始前的情况
截然不同。中国人在沿江沉没或
漂浮了数千枚水雷，在江阴、
乌龙山、马当、石磊窑和团风
设置了封锁线，并建立了坚固的
防御工事加以保护。日本军队
通过溯江作战，以巨大的牺牲
克服了中国军队的顽强抵抗，
从而为己方航运开通了河道。
**‘巨大牺牲’**
“假设日本军队在没有打破
中国人设置的封锁线的情况下
继续作战。没有任何第三国
能够尝试在长江航行，至少
在敌对行动期间是这样。
“日本军队开通长江是为了
执行其作战任务。我们认为，
那些在中国军队出于敌对目的
封锁河道时未采取有效措施
加以制止的第三国，现在必须
能够认识到这样一个事实：日本
军队完全是为了其军事目的，
以巨大牺牲完成了河道的开通。

"Stick To Decision"
"The hostilities have not come to
an end yet. The operations are
still continually going on, and the
Yangtse, even now that the Wu-
han area is under our control, is
part of the battle field and con-
stitutes an artery of replenish-
ment which is of great importance
for our operations. The Japanese
forces are making great efforts to
secure themselves against the
obstructions put up by the Chin-
ese forces.
"A large number of Japanese
vessels now navigating the Yang-
tse River are engaged in the
transportation of munitions and
such articles as are necessary for
the maintenance of the Japanese
forces and organizations attached
to them, and no vessel is engaged
in general trade.
"It is needless to say that the
Japanese operating forces earnest-
ly desire that as the necessity of
executing military operations in
Central China decrease, such a
state of affairs may speedily be
restored as will enable the Powers
concerned to enjoy trading on the
Yangtse. The present situation,
however, is far from our wish, and
we shall be compelled to stick to
our decision as long as the Chin-
ese forces maintain their present
attitude."
page_data.zh:
**‘坚持决定’**
“敌对行动尚未结束。作战
仍在持续进行，即使武汉地区
已在我们的控制之下，长江仍是
战场的一部分，并构成对我们
作战至关重要的补给动脉。
日本军队正大力努力确保自身
免受中国军队设置的障碍之害。
“目前在长江航行的众多日本
船只从事的是弹药及维持日本
军队及其附属组织所需物资的
运输，没有一艘船只从事一般
贸易。
“毋庸赘言，日本作战部队
真诚地希望，随着在华中华地区
执行军事行动的必要性减少，
能够迅速恢复使有关列强得以
在长江享受贸易的状况。然而，
目前的局势远非我们所愿，只
要中国军队保持目前的态度，
我们将被迫坚持我们的决定。”

December 27, 1938. Morning Translation

Hwa Mei Chen Pao and other local newspapers :-

CLOSING OF YANGTSE AND PEARL RIVERS

According to information secured by a reporter of
the Fleet News Agency, a certain reliable official organiza-
tion in this locality, which has close connections with the
trade between China and the Powers, has received reports from
many quarters to the effect that Japan is determined to close
the Yangtse and Pearl Rivers to foreign shipping. The
reports state that in closing these two waterways Japan is
attempting to monopolize the markets in these two valleys
and to banish vessels of Britain, America and other third
Powers from operating along these two rivers, thereby
eliminating foreign trade in China, through her puppet
regimes which, should Japan succeed in conquering China,
will be instructed to claim the restoration of the inland
navigation rights to China.
The British, American and French senior members
of this official organization have submitted the above
reports to their respective governments for their information.

in monopolizing trade in the occupied areas and in
