December 14, 1938. Afternoon Translation

Chinese American Daily News and other local newspapers :-

BRITISH AND AMERICAN RESIDENTS ANXIOUS OVER JAPANESE
MONOPOLY OF SHIPPING ALONG YANGTSE

In an attempt to monopolize navigation along
the Yangtse, the Japanese authorities have formed a
"Yangtse River Steam Navigation Company" (揚子江輪船公司)
to commence operations as from January 1 next year.
Upon learning of this, local British and
American residents became anxious. They hold the view
that if navigation along the Yangtse be monopolized by
the Japanese, the trade as well as the interests of foreign
Powers in China would be seriously affected and jeopardized.
For this reason, local foreign residents are paying close
attention to the matter and will hold a joint meeting at
the British Chamber of Commerce on the evening of
December 15 to consider the situation.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao of December 13 published the following letter:-

NATIONAL FLAG TO BE HOISTED ON SUNDAYS

To the Editor,
Lately a strange thing has occurred. The
Customs House is flying a "five-barred flag". Everybody
except traitors, upon seeing it, sighs with grief.
If we are determined to protect our country
and to support the war of resistance, we can do like the
soldiers at the front by displaying our lovely Chinese
national flag early every Sunday, especially from the
tops of lofty skyscrapers.
Waung Foong (汪風).

Ta Ying Yeh Pao of December 13 :-

NEW GAMBLING DEN TO BE ESTABLISHED IN HONGKEW

A certain party has leased a large and
spacious hotel on North Szechuan Road for use as a
gambling den similar to those in the Western District.
The preparations have been going on for more
than a month already but owing to the question of passes
it cannot be opened yet.
This gambling den will be operated as a club.

Chinese American Daily News and other local newspapers :-

SHOOTING AFFRAY IN A GAMBLING DEN

Shortly after 6 p.m. December 12, a number
of loafers, three of whom were armed with pistols, appeared
at the Dah Sun Gambling Den (大生賭窟), Shing Kong Li
(新康里) on Jessfield Road in the Western District, and
made an attempt to deprive a leading gambler named Ma Ts-
chi (馬自琪) of his money. When Ma resisted, the loafers
opened fire and decamped. Ma who was wounded in the left
arm was sent to hospital by policemen of the puppet regime.

1938年12月14日。下午译件

《中美日报》及其他本地报纸：

英美侨民对日本垄断长江航运感到焦虑

为企图垄断长江航行，日本当局已组建“扬子江轮船公司”（揚子江輪船公司），定于明年1月1日开始运营。获悉此事后，本地英美侨民深感焦虑。他们认为，如果长江航行被日本垄断，在华外国列强的贸易及利益将受到严重影响和损害。因此，本地外侨正密切关注此事，并将于12月15日晚在英国商会举行联席会议，以商讨局势。

12月13日的《大英夜报》刊登了以下来信：

周日悬挂国旗

致编辑：

Ta Mei Pao published the following editorial on Dec.18 :-

WHY JAPAN REFUSES TO OPEN THE YANGTSZE

Thus far, the Japanese Government has refused
to admit that its action in closing the Yangtsze to public
navigation is due to economic and political reasons,
although they allege that it is due to military reasons.
In the course of a speech on the Yangtsze
navigation issue made after his return to Japan from an
inspection tour in China, Chuso Mitsuchi, a so-called
veteran Japanese statesman stated: "At the present
moment, Japan cannot concede the Yangtsze navigation
issue. If Japan should yield now, the heavy sacrifice
she has made would be nullified."
This is indeed plain talk for it makes known
to the public that Japan's refusal to open the Yangtsze
to public navigation is due to economic motives and not **〔此处转录不清〕**
because of military exigencies. The so-called "heavy
sacrifice" of course refers to economic interests and not
to military operations.
As regards the possibility of Britain, America
and France resorting to retaliatory measures against Japan,
the Japanese statesman said: "If the Powers should
retaliate with economic measures, Japan has only to
strike at Shanghai, which, in the eyes of the Powers, is
a precious child."
Is Shanghai really such a precious child to
the Powers? If this is the case, then it is indeed
very good news to us because, in our opinion, Shanghai
is not a precious child at all, but a miserable orphan.
If Japan can do something to enable the Powers to look
after their residents in Shanghai, as in the case of a
precious child, then we should be very happy.

《大美报》于12月18日发表以下社论：

日本为何拒绝开放长江

迄今为止，日本政府虽声称其封闭长江禁止公共航行是出于军事原因，但拒绝承认此举是出于经济和政治原因。
一位所谓的日本资深政治家光中忠三（Chuso Mitsuchi，音译）在结束对华视察返回日本后，就长江航行问题发表演讲称：“目前，日本不能在长江航行问题上让步。如果日本现在屈服，其所作出的巨大牺牲将化为乌有。”
这确实是直言不讳，因为它向公众表明，日本拒绝开放长江供公共航行是出于经济动机，而非**〔此处转录不清〕**因为军事急需。所谓的“巨大牺牲”当然指的是经济利益，而非军事行动。
关于英、美、法可能对日本采取报复措施的可能性，这位日本政治家表示：“如果列强采取经济措施进行报复，日本只需打击上海，而在列强眼中，上海是一个宠儿。”
上海对列强来说真的是这样的宠儿吗？如果是这样，那对我们来说确实是个好消息，因为在我们看来，上海根本不是什么宠儿，而是一个可怜的孤儿。如果日本能做些什么，让列强像对待宠儿一样照顾他们在上海的居民，那我们将非常高兴。

Standard and other local newspapers :-

NAVIGATION ALONG THE YANGTZE

The Lower Yangtze from the Kiangyin Forts
upwards has been closed to navigation since the fall of
Nanking and Hangchow, but Japanese goods have been
transported in large quantities to occupied areas under
the cloak of military requirements. As the control of
transportation and navigation along the Yangtze is in
their hands, the Japanese authorities have acquired a
rare opportunity for the extensive disposal of their
goods.

As the Yangtze is closely related to the
prosperity of the interior districts of China and with
a view to bringing about a complete control of navigation
along this river, the Japanese authorities have already
started preparations to establish a large shipping company
in Shanghai with a capital of $10,000,000 to engage
exclusively in navigation and transportation business
along the Yangtze River.

Recently a meeting was held at the Japanese
Club in Hongkew, at which a Chairman of the Board of
Directors of the company was elected and the date for its
formal inauguration was fixed. Its offices will be located
in the Mitsui Bank Building. In addition to the Yangtze,
the company, after its formal establishment, will also
assume control of navigation along other rivers. The
Powers, especially Britain and the U.S.A., will suffer
more losses.

At present only boats belonging to
the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, a Japanese shipping concern,
are allowed to pass through the Kiangyin Boom; the
steamers of Butterfield & Swire and of the Indo-China
Steam Navigation Company, Ltd. can only sail between
Shanghai and Tiensunkiang (天生港). The Nisshin Kisen
Kaisha is building four 1,200-ton steamers for the
Yangtze service.

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

长江航行

自南京和杭州沦陷以来，江阴要塞以上的长江下游已禁止航行，但日本货物借军事需求之名，大量运往占领区。由于长江运输和航行的控制权掌握在他们手中，日本当局获得了大规模处置其货物的难得机会。

鉴于长江与中国内地地区的繁荣息息相关，且为了实现对这条河流航行的完全控制，日本当局已开始准备在上海成立一家大型航运公司，资本为一千万美元，专门从事长江沿线的航行和运输业务。

最近在虹口日本俱乐部举行了一次会议，选举了该公司董事会主席，并确定了正式成立的日期。其办事处将设在三井银行大楼。除长江外，该公司正式成立后还将接管其他河流的航行控制。列强，尤其是英国和美国，将遭受更多损失。

目前，只有属于日本航运公司日清汽船株式会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）的船只被允许通过江阴封锁线；太古洋行（Butterfield & Swire）和印度支那轮船公司有限公司（Indo-China Steam Navigation Company, Ltd.）的轮船只能在上海和天生港（Tiensunkiang）之间航行。日清汽船株式会社正在为长江航线建造四艘1200吨级的轮船。

BLOCKADE OF YANGTSZE RIVER NOT JUSTIFIED AT PRESENT

As the Japanese have blockaded the Yangtsze
River, British shipping circles on December 1 sent three
representatives to make an inspection along the Yangtsze.
They returned to Shanghai on December 15.
According to a report made by the three
representatives, no mines were found along the Yangtsze
from Nanking to Hankow, while Japanese steamers were
noticed navigating the river without trouble The report
states that the blockade of the Yangtsze is unnecessary
and declares that the refusal on the part of the Japanese
to re-open the Yangtsze is not justified.
British shipping concerns have compiled a
report on the basis of this inspection and will send it
to the British Consulate with a request for further
negotiations with the Japanese authorities.

Humanity ( 人类 ), a semi-monthly magazine, of December 16 is-
HOW FOREIGN POWERS MAY SAFEGUARD THEIR INTERESTS IN CHINA

Japan has blockaded the Yangtse River and
prohibits ships of a third Power from sailing on it.
Great Britain and America have lodged protests with Japan
against the blockade.
According to information secured from an
unofficial source, Japan intends to withdraw from the
Nine-Power Pact. She has hinted that she will not
respect the principle of the open door policy. It is
also reported that Japan will establish a United Government
in China and instigate it to call on the Chinese people
to resist the Imperialists of the Western countries, with the
object of driving away the influence of third Powers from
China.
Japan holds the opinion that the principle
of the open door policy is deeply impressed upon the minds
of the Powers. In order to close the door of China,
the first thing she has to do is to wipe out all ideas
about this principle from the minds of the people of
Western countries. When Western people cease to insist
upon the maintenance of the principle of the open door,
Japan may then occupy China without trouble.
The Powers should realize that their rights
and interests in China are safe only so long as China is
independent. Should China lose her independence, these
rights and interests will be lost to them. Therefore,
the Powers must first preserve the independence of China.
This is clearly outlined in the Washington Nine-Power Pact.
Since the Mukden Incident, Japan has been
impairing the independence of China and ignored her
obligations as defined in the Nine-Power Pact. The Powers
have failed to adopt effective sanctions against Japan's
acts of violation of the independence of China. Thus,
it would seem that the Powers themselves have failed to
observe their obligations under this Pact. The Powers
have now lodged protests against Japan's violation of
their interests in China; their attitude towards Japan
has changed.
If the Powers desire to maintain their rights
and interests in China, they must first adopt effective
measures to assure the independence of China.

12月16日的半月刊《人类》（Humanity）：

外国列强如何保障其在华利益

日本封锁了长江，并禁止第三国船舶在其上航行。英国和美国已就封锁一事向日本提出抗议。
据从非官方渠道获得的消息，日本打算退出《九国公约》。她暗示将不尊重门户开放政策的原则。另有报道说，日本将在中国建立一个联合政府，并唆使其号召中国人民抵抗西方国家的帝国主义者，目的是将第三势力的影响驱逐出中国。
日本认为，门户开放政策的原则在列强心中根深蒂固。为了关闭中国的大门，她首先要做的就是从西方国家人民的脑海中抹去关于这一原则的所有想法。当西方人不再坚持维护门户开放原则时，日本便可毫无麻烦地占领中国。
列强应认识到，只有在中国独立的情况下，他们在华的权利和利益才是安全的。如果中国失去独立，这些权利和利益也将随之丧失。因此，列强必须首先保持中国的独立。这在华盛顿《九国公约》中有明确阐述。
自沈阳事变以来，日本一直在损害中国的独立，并无视其在《九国公约》中规定的义务。列强未能对日本侵犯中国独立的行为采取有效制裁。因此，似乎列强自身也未能遵守该公约下的义务。列强现已就日本侵犯其在华利益提出抗议；他们对日本的态度发生了改变。
如果列强希望维持其在华的权利和利益，他们必须首先采取有效措施以确保中国的独立。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
DEC 2 1938

Japanese To Maintain Status Quo
On Yangtze, Navy Office Official
Asserts; Statement Upholds Local
Declaration Of Nippon Spokesmen

Arms Smuggling
On Foreign Ship
Cited In Tokyo

Allegation About Arms
Supplied Guerillas
Gets Support

CHINESE BOARD
FOREIGN SHIPS

Japanese River Trade
Continues; Cargoes
Varied

(Domei)
TOKYO, Dec. 2. — Japanese military authorities will be compelled to maintain the status quo of the Yangtze River" as long as the Chinese armies persist in their present attitude," Rear-Admiral Masso Kanazawa, Chief of the Navy Office, declared last night.
He made the statement in upholding a joint declaration by spokesmen of the Japanese Army and Navy headquarters in Shanghai regarding the question of free navigation on the river.

**Steamer Wangtung**
Referring to allegations that arms and ammunition were supplied to Chinese guerillas by foreign vessels operating in the estuary of the Yangtze open to free navigation, and instances of reported interference with foreign vessels by Chinese guerillas, Rear-Admiral Kanazawa recalled the case of the steamer Wangtung owned by the Butterfield & Swire Company.

**Ammunition Found**
When the vessel entered Shanghai November 29, Rear-Admiral Kanazawa said, 8000 rounds of ammunition and two guns allegedly were found on board.
An Italian ship arrived in Shanghai October 7 with 10 armed Chinese soldiers on board, the spokesman said.
Chinese guerillas boarded a British steamer near Shanghai November 24 and threatened the officers, Rear-Admiral Kanazawa stated.

**Seizures Made**
According to local police and court evidence, the Wantung, when boarded last Tuesday in the river by Customs officers, was found to be carrying 800 rounds of ammunition, not 8000, and no guns were mentioned. No arrests were made.

The ship trades between here and Chitung and Haimen, on the north Yangtze bank, and authorities believe the ammunition was being smuggled to bandits on Tsungming Island.
On the same day a Chinese was arrested on the Bund with 5000 rounds of rifle ammunition, two Mausers and 50 rounds of Mauser ammunition, the supplies having been taken off the Portuguese steamer Faro, which was sailing for Tsungming.

**Goods Shipped**
At various times bandits and pirates have attacked foreign vessels in the lower Yangtze in the past several months. Latest reported attacks were made by pirates on two Japanese merchant ships below the Kiangyin boom, and it is understood that both captains are being held for ransom. Allegations have been made that in several instances these attacks have been made by guerillas, but these have not been confirmed.
Meanwhile Japanese vessels continue to transport cargo from Shanghai to up-river ports, this cargo not being generally considered of military nature, though the Japanese insist that all goods are for army and rehabilitation purposes. Kowan, west of Kiangyin, is the center of the trade. Goods transported by many vessels up and down river in the last few days have included piece goods, sugar, paper, sundries, wheat, sandalwood, vegetable tallow, albumen, medicine, eggs, egg products, dried lilies, yolk, melon seeds, cotton yarn, sesamum seed, sea products, oil, tobacco stalk and leaf, white nuts, etc.

东京，12月2日电。——海军省厅长金泽增夫（Masso Kanazawa，音译）少将昨晚宣称，“只要中国军队坚持目前的态度”，日本军事当局将被迫“维持长江的现状”。
他发表此声明是为了支持日本陆军和海军上海总部发言人关于长江自由航行问题的联合宣言。

**“广东”号轮船**
针对有关在开放自由航行的长江口水域运营的外国船只向中国游击队提供武器弹药的指控，以及有关中国游击队干涉外国船只的报道案例，金泽少将回顾了太古洋行所有的“广东”号（Wangtung）轮船一案。

**发现弹药**
金泽少将称，当该船于11月29日进入上海时，据称在船上发现了8000发子弹和两门枪。
发言人称，一艘意大利船只于10月7日抵达上海，船上有10名武装中国士兵。
金泽少将称，11月24日，中国游击队在靠近上海的地方登上了一艘英国轮船，并威胁船员。

**实施扣押**
根据当地警方和法庭证据，上周二海关官员在江上登临“广东”号（Wantung，原文拼写有误，应指前文Wangtung）时，发现其携带800发子弹，而非8000发，且未提及枪支。无人被捕。
该船在此地与长江北岸的启东（Chitung，音译）和海门之间贸易，当局认为这些弹药正被走私给崇明岛上的匪徒。
同日，一名中国人在外滩被捕，身上藏有5000发步枪子弹、两支毛瑟枪和50发毛瑟枪子弹，这些物资是从驶往崇明的葡萄牙轮船“法罗”号（Faro）上卸下的。

**货物运输**
在过去几个月里，匪徒和海盗曾多次在下长江袭击外国船只。据报道，最近的袭击是海盗在江阴封锁线下方对两艘日本商船进行的，据悉两名船长均被扣留以索取赎金。有人指控这些袭击在几起案件中是由游击队所为，但尚未得到证实。
与此同时，日本船只继续将货物从上海运往上游港口，这些货物通常不被视为具有军事性质，尽管日本人坚持所有货物均用于军队和重建目的。江阴以西的口岸（Kowan，音译）是贸易中心。过去几天许多船只上下运输的货物包括匹头、糖、纸张、杂货、小麦、檀香木、植物油、蛋白、药品、鸡蛋、蛋制品、百合干、蛋黄、瓜子、棉纱、芝麻、海产品、油、烟梗和烟叶、白果等。

Ta Mei Pao (Editorial) :-

FOREIGNERS AND JAPANESE RESTRICTIONS ON TRADE

The increased restrictions placed by the Japanese authorities on foreign trade has given rise to much indignation among foreigners. The foreigners have now entered into a strong pact of co-operation and something will be done to demonstrate the strength of their unity.

Ten important local foreign bodies are said to have issued manifestoes outlining their position and have made certain suggestions in an attempt to bring about the removal of all the obstructions to foreign trade. They have also demanded the safeguarding of foreign interests in China under international treaties.

This action on the part of the foreigners constitutes one of the most positive movements that have taken place during the past few weeks. We have received a report of the suggestions submitted by these ten foreign bodies which include the American Residents' Association, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the Belgian Chamber of Commerce, the British Chamber of Commerce, the British Residents' Association, the Federation of British Residents in China, the Shanghai Canadian Club, the French Chamber of Commerce, the Norwegian Chamber of Commerce and the Swedish Chamber of Commerce, to their respective governments. There may be other proposals in addition to these, but owing to the complicated nature of international politics, we consider it inappropriate to publish all of them.

The objects of these foreign bodies are:-
(1) To maintain all their rights and to prevent all trespass and interference with the administration of the International Settlement and the French Concession in accordance with the Yangkingpang Land Regulations. They will also endeavour to bring about the immediate removal of all menace to their rights.

《大美报》（社论）：-

外人与日本对贸易的限制

日本当局对外国贸易施加的日益增多的限制，已在外人中引起极大愤慨。外人现已达成一项强有力的合作协定，并将采取某些行动以展示其团结的力量。

据悉，十个重要的本地外侨团体已发表宣言，阐明其立场，并提出若干建议，试图消除对外国贸易的所有障碍。他们还要求根据国际条约保障外国在华利益。

外人的这一举动构成了过去几周内发生的最积极的运动之一。我们收到了这十个外侨团体向其各自政府提交的建议报告，这些团体包括：美国居留民会、美国商会、比利时商会、英国商会、英国居留民会、在华英人联合会、上海加拿大人俱乐部、法国商会、挪威商会和瑞典商会。除这些建议外，可能还有其他提议，但由于国际政治的复杂性，我们认为不宜全部刊登。

这些外侨团体的目标如下：
(1) 维护其所有权利，防止任何侵犯及根据《洋泾浜土地章程》对公共租界和法租界行政管理的干涉。他们还将努力促使立即消除对其权利的所有威胁。

(4) 促使取消违反《九国公约》所规定的门户开放政策和机会均等原则而建立的所有垄断。
(5) 要求立即将所有被扣押财产归还原主。
(6) 要求停止对邮件和电报的检查，以及任何第三方对所有其他通讯的干涉。
(7) 要求立即归还所有疏浚设备并恢复航道治理工作，以便上海能够维持国际航运。
(8) 坚持这些国家的居民有权享有的一切权利和特权，使他们能够在机会均等的原则下开展合法经营。
(9) 要求承认并维持这些国家居民所享有的领事裁判权。
日本当局在拒绝给予他人优惠权利时提出的唯一借口是所谓的“反日政策”。说实话，日本当局的行为毫无理由，只能被视为一种排外政策。这种政策不仅自私且愚蠢，而且也是自杀性的，因为该政策同样损害日本自身的利益。
日本当局一再要求外人保持耐心，但外人感到失望和沮丧。只有采取一致行动，他们今天才能取得更好的结果。我们已经吸取了痛苦的教训，即没有行动的无限耐心是无用的，如果他们希望保护自己的利益，现在就是采取强力行动的时候。

SHANGHAI TIMES

NOV 20 1938

ONE JAPANESE VIEW
ON YANGTZE

Editor,
THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES
Sir,—Since Japan has rejected lately the demand made by Great Britain, United States of America and France, in respect to the Yangtze river navigation, many arguments, viewpoints, complaints or explanations are reported daily in the papers. However, from my personal point of view, none of them seems to have realized the vital point on this question.
The vital point referred to is this; Soon after the current hostilities started, Chinese military authorities closed and blockaded the Yangtze river navigation for shipping of any nationality. Against this, none of the third parties has made proper protest within my knowledge. This means; the navigable river of Yangtze does not exist anymore so far as the rights or interests of the third parties are concerned. Their right in question has been completely waived according to the technical construction of international law. The right of the third parties on the Yangtze river navigation was conferred or recognized by the Chinese National Government, and it became virtually null and void, or at least was indefinitely ceased to exist, by the fact of blockade done by the Chinese military authorities. It must be minded that the status of blockade is still existing so far as the third parties are concerned, which Japan has nothing to do with the removal of blockade done by Japanese force.
Japanese spokesmen say; “The river has been reopened solely for military purpose, the navigation of the third parties’ shipping is still dangerous, shipping facilities are not available, or so on.” However, these explanations are not proper and are reliable to be taken as an unprincipled excuse for Japanese monopoly of Yangtze river trade. Those spokesmen seem to have not clearly realized real Japanese stand

in this connection.
It can be taken as generally accepted that, apart from the political cause of the current Sino-Japanese conflicts, the Yangtze river trade has been blockaded against Japan by the Chiang’s regime. And when booms and mines were laid down, the river trade of the third parties was concurrently blockaded. It is to be sympathized with the third parties whose rights and interests have been completely destroyed on account of this. Now, Japan has removed the Chinese blockade of Yangtze river by force for her own interest, at the expense of tremendous cost of war operations.
For such Japanese work, those third parties, who are now protesting against Japan, have not only rendered any collaboration, but they even showed certain objection. From these vital facts, third parties are in no way entitled to claim to benefit themselves of the re-opening of Yangtze river. From lawful construction, the river is still in the condition blockaded by China but not by Japan, and no navigable river of Yangtze exists now, so far as the third parties are concerned. How Japan may utilize the navigation of Yangtze river for military purpose or for commercial purpose, it is Japan’s own business. No third party can say anything against it.
The same construction can be applied to the cases of Ports of Tsingtao, Canton and Amoy, as these ports have been closed and blockaded by Chinese for any foreign shipping when booms and mines were laid down, and the lawful status of blockade will be indefinitely continued, or the function of open ports ceased to exist. The removal of booms and mines by Japanese force does not affect at all the said status of the ports.
TONAN.
Shanghai, November 16, 1938.

《字林西报》

1938年11月20日

关于长江的一种日本观点

致：
《上海星期泰晤士报》编辑
先生，——自从日本最近拒绝了英国、美国和法国关于长江航行的要求以来，报纸上每天都报道许多论点、观点、抱怨或解释。然而，从我个人的角度来看，它们似乎都没有认识到这个问题的关键点。
所指的关键点在于；在当前敌对行动开始后不久，中国军事当局关闭并封锁了长江航行，禁止任何国籍的船只通行。据我所知，没有任何第三方对此提出适当的抗议。这意味着；就第三方的权利或利益而言，长江可航河流已不复存在。根据国际法的技术性解释，他们的有关权利已被完全放弃。第三方在长江航行上的权利是由中国国民政府授予或承认的，而由于中国军事当局实施封锁的事实，这些权利实际上已失效，或者至少无限期地停止存在。必须注意的是，就第三方而言，封锁状态仍然存在，日本与解除由其武力实施的封锁无关。
日本发言人称：“重新开放河道纯粹出于军事目的，第三方船只的航行仍然危险，航运设施不可用，等等。”然而，这些解释并不恰当，只能被视为日本垄断长江贸易的无原则借口。这些发言人似乎没有清楚地认识到日本在此问题上的真实立场。

普遍认为，除了当前中日冲突的政治原因外，长江贸易已被蒋政权对日本封锁。当设置水栅和水雷时，第三方的河运也同时被封锁。那些因之权利和利益被彻底摧毁的第三方值得同情。现在，日本为了自身利益，以巨大的战争行动成本为代价，用武力解除了中国对长江的封锁。
对于日本的这项工作，那些现在抗议日本的第三方不仅没有提供任何合作，甚至表现出某种反对。从这些关键事实来看，第三方无权声称从长江的重新开放中获益。从法律解释来看，该河流仍处于由中国而非日本封锁的状态，就第三方而言，现在不存在可航行的长江。日本如何利用长江航行用于军事或商业目的，是日本自己的事。任何第三方都无权对此提出异议。
同样的解释也适用于青岛、广州和厦门港口的情况，因为这些港口在设置水栅和水雷时已被中国人对所有外国航运关闭和封锁，封锁的法律状态将无限期持续，或者开放港口的功能已停止存在。日本用武力清除水栅和水雷完全不影响上述港口的地位。
TONAN.
上海，1938年11月16日。

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 20 1938

Japan’s Reply
To Note Said
“Insult To
Intelligence”

American Residents In
Shanghai Show Sharp
Reaction To Note

BRITONS ASSAIL
TOKYO ‘DISGUISE’

“Real Reply Between
The Lines,” Says
Leading Merchant

American business men in Shanghai reacted sharply yesterday to Tokyo's decision against the reopening of the Yangtse and the discontinuance of restrictions against foreign traders in the occupied zones, as expressed in the Japanese reply to Mr. Cordell Hull's note of October 6.

Terse, and to the point, American opinion was supported by British traders, several of whom expressed the hope that the Tokyo reply would have the immediate effect of hastening joint action by America, Britain and France on the subject of the note.

Lack Of Originality

“To any American fully acquainted with the facts of Japanese aggression in China, the Japanese reply to the American note of October 6 can only be regarded as an insult to the intelligence of the American people, declared one of Shanghai's most prominent American merchants in an interview with THE CHINA PRESS yesterday.

“The Japanese reply,” he added “only once again depicts the lack of originality so often shown by that nation, in as much as it follows exactly the course used by the Japanese in swallowing Manchuria.”

“Sweet Words”

Said another American business man, closely connected with internal trade in China, “The Japanese reply to Washington's note was what we expected. I do not think that Tokyo has justified in any way, the restrictions which have been imposed on foreign trade in China. It seems that the Japanese Foreign Office was created for the purpose of keeping us quiescent with sweet words until they get us where they want us.”

British opinion, as canvassed by THE CHINA PRESS, was best expressed by the leading member of a well-known firm of traders in Shanghai. “The real reply may be read between the lines, ingeniously camouflaged by a cleverly constructed, but naive line of argument. I have never read so much nonsense.”

《密勒氏评论报》
1938年11月20日

日本对照会的答复
被称为
“对智商的侮辱”

上海美国居留民
对照会反应强烈

英国人抨击
东京的“伪装”

“真正的答复
藏在字里行间，”一位
主要商人说

昨天，上海美国商人对东京决定不重新开放长江并继续在被占领区对外国商人实施限制的反应强烈，这一决定体现在日本对科德尔·赫尔先生10月6日照会的答复中。

简洁而切中要害的美国观点得到了英国商人的支持，其中几人表示希望东京的答复能立即产生效果，加速美、英、法三国就照会事项采取联合行动。

缺乏新意

“对于任何充分了解日本在华侵略事实的美国人来说，日本对10月6日美国照会的答复只能被视为对美国人民智商的侮辱，”上海一位最杰出的美国商人在昨天接受《密勒氏评论报》采访时宣称。

他补充说：“日本的答复再次描绘了该国经常表现出的缺乏新意，因为它完全遵循了日本吞并满洲时所采用的路线。”

“甜言蜜语”

另一位与中国国内贸易密切相关的美国商人说：“日本对华盛顿照会的答复正如我们所料。我认为东京完全没有为其在中国对外贸易中施加的限制提供正当理由。看来日本外务省的设立目的就是用甜言蜜语让我们保持安静，直到他们把我们带到他们想要的位置。”

《密勒氏评论报》征询的英国舆论，最好地由上海一家知名贸易公司的主要成员表达。“真正的答复可以透过字里行间读到，它被巧妙构建但幼稚的论点巧妙地伪装起来。我从未读过如此多的废话。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOV 20 1938
Japan Firm in
Refusal to
Open Yangtze
Fear Foreigners May
Trade With Guerillas
"Military necessity" remained a paramount factor in determining the attitude of the Japanese military and naval authorities regarding Yangtze navigation, Japanese military, naval and diplomatic spokesmen in Shanghai emphasized yesterday, as the question of allowing foreign merchantmen to proceed up the river was again aired at a press conference.
The possibility that foreign merchantmen, if permitted to use the river, would engage in trading with guerillas and other Chinese, opposing the Japanese forces, was cited by the military spokesman as an additional deterrent to the Japanese to reopen the Yangtze to commercial vessels owned and operated by third party nationals.
Such activities, the spokesman said, could easily lead to "serious complications" which the Japanese authorities were seeking to avoid.
No More Incidents
"There have been a number of unfortunate and unpleasant incidents on the river. We intend to prevent another repetition," he said.
Chinese irregulars, a naval spokesman admitted, were still active at points as close to Shanghai as the Kiangyin boom.
"Military necessity is therefore compelling us to place the river, along which fighting is still going on, under Japanese control," he declared.
Recalling that the Powers had not taken "any effective measures" to prevent the Chinese from sinking various booms in the Yangtze, thereby cutting off this avenue of traffic, in addition to strongly mining the entire waterway, the naval spokesman declared that "it seems to me, it is a little too selfish" of third party Powers to demand that their ships be allowed to ply the river now that the Japanese had opened a channel.
This passage, he emphasized, was for "military purposes."
No Effective Measures
When a correspondent remarked that the Powers had protested to China against the closing of the river, the spokesman declared: "Yes, but they did not take any effective measures."
The spokesmen denied that the attitude now being taken by the Japanese authorities constituted a "blockade" of the river to third party shipping.
Admitting, in reply to a question, that produce from various river ports was being brought to Shanghai by Japanese vessels, the naval spokesman insisted that these goods were being consumed by the military.
"Eggs, for instance. We have men in barracks, in camps and in hospital who eat eggs," he said.
The presence of an estimated 200,-000 men "bandits, guerillas and irregulars" in an area bounded by Hangchow in the south, Shanghai in the east, and Nanking in the west, was admitted by a military spokesman. "There are many more of them along the river and inland, upstream from Nanking," he said.

《字林西报》，
1938年11月20日

日本坚决拒绝
开放长江
担心外国人可能与游击队进行贸易

上海方面的日本陆、海及外交界发言人昨日强调，在决定日本军方和海军当局对长江航运的态度时，“军事必要性”仍然是一个首要因素，当时允许外国商船溯江而上的问题再次在记者招待会上被提出。

军方发言人指出，如果允许外国商船使用长江，它们可能会与游击队及其他反对日军的中国势力进行贸易，这种可能性是日本方面不愿向第三国国民拥有和经营的商船重新开放长江的另一个阻碍因素。

该发言人称，此类活动很容易导致“严重复杂局面”，而这正是日本当局试图避免的。

不再发生事故

“江上已发生过多起不幸且令人不愉快的事件。我们打算防止此类事件再次发生，”他说。

一位海军发言人承认，中国非正规军甚至在靠近上海的江阴封锁线附近等地依然活跃。

“因此，军事必要性迫使我们将对仍在进行战斗的这条河流置于日本控制之下，”他宣称。

这位海军发言人回顾说，列强并未采取“任何有效措施”来阻止中国人在长江沉没各种封锁障碍物，从而切断这条交通要道，此外还在整个水道布设了大量水雷；他宣称，“在我看来，既然日本人已经开辟了一条通道，第三国列强却要求允许其船只在这条河流上航行，这未免有些自私。”

他强调，这条通道是用于“军事目的”的。

无有效措施

当一名记者指出列强曾就封闭长江一事向中国提出抗议时，该发言人宣称：“是的，但他们没有采取任何有效措施。”

发言人们否认日本当局目前采取的态度构成了对第三国航运的长江“封锁”。

在回答提问时，这位海军发言人承认，来自各沿江港口的农产品正由日本船只运往上海，但他坚持认为这些物资供军队消费。

“例如鸡蛋。我们在兵营、营地和医院里的人员都吃鸡蛋，”他说。

一位军方发言人承认，在南至杭州、东至上海、西至南京的区域内，估计有20万名“匪徒、游击队和非正规军”。他说：“沿江及南京上游的内陆地区，这类人更多。”

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOV 1 8 1938

Japanese Deny Yangtze Trade
Only War Supplies Being Shipped on River.
Says Spokesman ; Fighters Being "Kept Happy"

ALL goods now being transported on the Yangtze, in addition to ordinary military equipment, are destined for consumption by the Japanese military and naval forces, Japanese spokesmen declared at a press conference yesterday. These shipments, it was pointed out, comprise a wide variety of goods as a huge army and navy must be fed, clothed and "kept happy." As a result commodities needed for the recreation and comfort of officers and men which are not part of the issued equipment but are purchased in canteens are being transported. Sold in canteens were in addition to canned food, beer, sake and other goods, commodities like cigarettes, flashlights, and matches, the spokesmen said.

All Japanese vessels operating on the Yangtze, the spokesmen continued, were acting under the orders of the Army or Navy Quartermasters' Corps. Specific permits were required for any shipment destined for a canteen at the front.

A varied range of commodities, including matches, cigarettes, and candles, the spokesmen continued, were being purchased in Shanghai where those goods were found to be cheaper or more abundant than in Japan.

None of the goods shipped on these vessels were being permitted to be sold to the Chinese.

The ships, a naval spokesman said, returned to Japan "virtually empty." Sometimes they were loaded with war booty, scrap iron or iron ore to be taken to Japan. Discarded military equipment and baggage" even that of foreign correspondents who were left in Hankow" was also being carried, he said.

No Commercial Cargo

The spokesman emphatically denied that commercial cargo, being shipped for private profit, was being carried.

Japanese commodities, the army spokesman admitted, were reaching Nanking by railway and also by canal route. The Shanghai-Nanking Railway, he added, was being operated as a military line and not as a commercial undertaking. As a result, permits were required for the transportation of goods.

Practical utility was the principal test for the granting of permits for the railway transportation of goods. This, the spokesman said, was "only natural", since the railway's present facilities were insufficient to carry all goods because of the pressure of military transport requirements.

Goods were also reaching Nanking from Shanghai by truck, he said.

All Official Transports

The various spokesmen insisted that all cargo for Yangtze ports came in official transports or in ships chartered by the Government. Asked to make a categorical denial that Japanese merchants were buying ordinary Chinese produce for shipment from Yangtze ports to Japan, no spokesman would do so. It was stated that it was very difficult for Japanese businessmen to purchase goods in the interior.

Although admitting that there were about 1,500 Japanese civilians along the Yangtze, it was asserted that all had some connection with the services, but some were conducting shops for the sale of Japanese goods to the troops. It was vaguely stated that Chinese could purchase Japanese goods in Nanking, but that these all came by rail or truck from Shanghai. Military permits had to be obtained before shipment.

A correspondent wished to know if foreign firms could obtain such permits and the spokesman thought it possible. The journalist then pointed out that he had made exhaustive investigation among American firms in Shanghai and could not find a single instance of a permit having been issued to American businessmen.

That beans and bristles were being shipped in Japanese vessels was emphasized by correspondents; this brought the reply that "it must be investigated."

Nature of Cargoes

As already reported in the "North-China Daily News," commodities taken up the Yangtze by Japanese ships include: Kerosene, piece goods, gasoline, tobacco stalk and leaf, cotton yarn, sandalwood, paper, sugar and sea products, charcoal, candles and tallow, soda ash and sundries. These same steamers returned from up-river ports with cargoes of wheat, eggs, seasamun seed, oil, albumin, yolk and other egg products, dried lilies, rice, melon seeds, and thousands of tons of such commodities as peas, feathers, medicines, beans, ramie, tea, hides and bristles, iron-ore and the usual Chinese vegetable products.

《字林西报》，
1938年11月18日

日本否认长江贸易
称江上仅运输军需物资。
发言人称：旨在让战斗人员“保持满意”

日本发言人在昨日的记者招待会上宣称，目前在长江运输的所有货物，除常规军事装备外，均 destined for（注定供）日本陆海军部队消费。有人指出，这些 shipments（装运物资）包含种类繁多的商品，因为庞大的陆海军必须得到食物供应、衣物供给并“保持满意”。因此，那些不属于配发装备、而是在小卖部购买的、供官兵娱乐和舒适所需的商品也在运输之列。发言人称，除了罐头食品、啤酒、清酒和其他物品外，在小卖部出售的还有香烟、手电筒和火柴等商品。

发言人们继续表示，所有在长江运营的日本船只均受陆军或海军军需部门的命令行事。任何运往前线小卖部的货物都需要特定的许可证。

发言人们接着说，包括火柴、香烟和蜡烛在内的各种商品正在上海采购，因为这些商品在上海比在日本更便宜或更充足。

这些船只运输的任何货物均不允许出售给中国人。

一位海军发言人说，这些船只返回日本时“几乎空载”。有时它们会装载战利品、废铁或铁矿石运往日本。他说，被丢弃的军事装备和行李——甚至包括留在汉口的外国记者的行李——也在运输之列。

无商业货物

该发言人 emphatically（坚决）否认船上载有为私人利润而运输的商业货物。

陆军发言人承认，日本商品正通过铁路以及运河路线运抵南京。他补充说，沪宁铁路正作为军事线路运营，而非商业经营。因此，货物运输需要许可证。

授予铁路货物运输许可证的主要标准是实际效用。这位发言人说，这是“很自然的”，因为由于军事运输需求的压力，铁路目前的设施不足以运输所有货物。

他说，货物也通过卡车从上海运抵南京。

均为官方运输

各位发言人坚持认为，运往长江各港口的所有货物均通过官方运输工具或由政府租用的船只运送。当被要求明确否认日本商人正在购买普通中国农产品以便从长江港口运往日本时，没有一位发言人愿意这样做。据称，日本商人在内地购买商品非常困难。

虽然承认长江沿线约有1,500名日本平民，但声称他们都与服务部门有某种联系，不过其中一些人开设商店，向部队出售日本商品。有人含糊地表示，中国人可以在南京购买日本商品，但这些商品全部通过铁路或卡车从上海运来。运输前必须获得军事许可证。

一名记者想知道外国公司能否获得此类许可证，发言人认为有可能。随后该记者指出，他对上海的美国公司进行了详尽调查，却找不到一例向美国商人颁发许可证的情况。

记者们强调，豆类 and 鬃毛正由日本船只运输；对此得到的答复是“必须进行调查”。

货物性质

正如《字林西报》此前报道的那样，日本船只溯长江而上运输的商品包括：煤油、匹头（布料）、汽油、烟梗和烟叶、棉纱、檀香木、纸张、糖和海产品、木炭、蜡烛和牛脂、苏打粉及杂项用品。这些轮船从上游港口返回时，装载着小麦、鸡蛋、芝麻籽、油、白蛋白、蛋黄和其他蛋制品、干百合、大米、瓜子，以及数以千吨计的豌豆、羽毛、药品、豆类、苎麻、茶叶、皮革和鬃毛、铁矿石和通常的中国蔬菜产品等商品。

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 16 1938

Japanese Merchant
Vessels Said Enjoying
Monopoly In Yangtse

Nipponese Firms Solicit
Chinese Cargo Freight
Through Agents

CHINESE PAPERS
CARRY DAILY “ADS”

Contention That River
Is Unsafe Said
Disproved

With foreign shipping barred from the Yangtse, Japanese merchantmen today enjoy unchallenged monopoly in Asia's most important waterway.

The Japanese Government's official contention, communicated to London, Paris and Washington on Monday, that the Yangtse River was closed to all but men-of-war, was belied by numerous advertisements appearing in local Chinese newspapers.

These advertisements, inserted by Chinese agents of Japanese shipping concerns, offered to transport goods and passengers to any port below Kiukiang "safely and speedily."

A survey conducted by THE CHINA PRESS revealed the following outstanding facts, the knowledge of which may vitally affect the Great Power's policy on the matter:

1. Japanese merchant ships are plying freely in the Yangtse;
2. No Japanese cargo or passenger, despite Tokyo's allegation that the river is still infested with mines, has met with any mishap; and
3. Japanese shipping firms are now enjoying in effect a monopoly on Yangtse shipping as a result of Tokyo's refusal to open the river to third-power merchantmen.

Agencies Advertise

The advertisements of these Chinese agents have been appearing regularly in at least one vernacular paper.

Altogether, there are half a dozen such agencies. They include the transportation department of the "Eastern Asia Industrial Company," the "Yung Lee Transportation Company," the "Tai-koo Chong Transportation Hong" and the "Hin Kee Water and Land Transportation Company".

Incidentally, the name of the Tai-koo Chong Hong is strikingly similar to the Chinese firm name of Butterfield and Swire, Merchants and Steamship Agents.

The advertisement of the Eastern Asia Company claims that the company specializes in shipping cargoes to Nanking, Wuhu, Chinkiang, Kiangyin, Kiukiang and Anking, and that it will obtain all necessary passes from Japanese authorities for the customers.

The offices of the company are significantly located on the third floor of the Yokohama Specie Bank Building.

Other advertisements appearing in the Chinese daily are quite similar in substance.

Contact By Phone

Chinese merchants who wish to contact these advertisers for information concerning the shipping of their cargoes can do so by telephone. Rate estimates would be quoted to customers over the wire, although final arrangements are dependent upon a personal inspection of the goods by a representative of the shipping agency.

To ship a bale of cotton to Wuhu, for instance, THE CHINA PRESS learned, would cost approximately $11 per ton. The quoted rates, however, are by no means final and may be lowered through bargaining.

Another arrangement is that no money need be paid by the Shanghai shipper. Since all of the agencies mentioned above claimed they have branches in the up-river ports, freight charges on the cargo may be collected at the other end of the line.

One significant thing about these Chinese agencies was that none of them knew—or at least would reveal—the name of the ship which would carry the cargo up-river. They confirmed, however, that all of the ships in such service are Japanese vessels.

Time Unknown

No agency could give the time required for bringing the goods to any of the specified ports. Shipping circles were of the opinion that since the Japanese military might requisition any Japanese commercial vessel, delays are quite explainable.

《大美晚报》，
1938年11月16日

称日本商船
在长江享有垄断地位

日本公司通过代理人
招揽中国货物运费

中文报纸
每日刊登“广告”

所谓河流不安全之说
据称已被驳斥

随着外国航运被禁止进入长江，日本商船如今在亚洲最重要的水道上享有无可挑战的垄断地位。

日本政府周一向伦敦、巴黎和华盛顿传达的官方主张——即长江除军舰外对所有船只关闭——与当地中文报纸上出现的大量广告相矛盾。

这些广告由日本航运公司的中国代理人刊登，承诺“安全迅速”地将货物和乘客运送至九江以下的任何港口。

《大美晚报》进行的一项调查揭示了以下突出事实，了解这些事实可能会严重影响列强在此事上的政策：

1. 日本商船在长江自由航行；
2. 尽管东京声称江上仍遍布水雷，但没有任何日本货物或乘客遭遇任何不幸；以及
3. 由于东京拒绝向第三国商船开放长江，日本航运公司实际上正在享受长江航运的垄断地位。

代理机构刊登广告

这些中国代理人的广告至少定期出现在一份中文报纸上。

总共有半打（约六家）这样的代理机构。其中包括“东亚实业公司”的运输部、“永利运输公司”、“太古昌运输行”和“兴记水陆运输公司”。

顺便提一下，“太古昌行”的名字与怡和洋行（Butterfield and Swire，商人和轮船代理商）的中文公司名称惊人地相似。

东亚公司的广告声称，该公司专门从事向南京、芜湖、镇江、江阴、九江和安庆运输货物，并将为客户从日本当局处获取所有必要的通行证。

该公司的办公室位于横滨正金银行大楼三楼，位置显著。

中文日报上出现的其他广告在实质内容上颇为相似。

电话联系

希望联系这些广告商以获取有关其货物运输信息的中国商人可以通过电话进行联系。虽然最终安排取决于航运代理机构代表对货物的亲自检查，但会通过电话向客户报价费率估算。

例如，《大美晚报》获悉，将一包棉花运往芜湖的费用约为每吨11美元。然而，所报费率绝非最终价格，可能通过议价降低。

另一种安排是，上海发货人无需支付任何费用。由于上述所有代理机构都声称在上游港口设有分支机构，货物的运费可以在航线的另一端收取。

这些中国代理机构的一个显著特点是，它们都不知道——或者至少不愿透露——将货物溯江而上的船只名称。但它们确认，提供此类服务的所有船只均为日本船只。

时间未知

没有任何代理机构能告知将货物运至任何指定港口所需的时间。航运界认为，由于日本军方可能会征用任何日本商业船只，延误是完全可以说得通的。

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 16 1938

Asked by a prospective customer one agency said that sailings up-river had been quite regular. One ship left Shanghai Monday morning, the prospective customer was informed.
All reports indicated that Japanese vessels, not exclusively men-of-war, had been plying the Yangtze River as far west as Kiukiang carrying cargoes for at least Chinese shippers.
This is a direct contradiction of the Japanese official statement that navigation on the Yangtze is only possible for military purposes.
This contention was made by the Japanese Government in its reply to Britain, France and the United States which recently demanded the reopening of the Yangtze river to foreign shipping.

American Note Strong
The American note, which was handed on October 6 to Premier Prince Ayamaro Konoye, who was then concurrently acting as Foreign Minister, by Mr Joseph Grew, U. S Ambassador in Tokyo, was the strongest of the three notes, and was the second American note to the Japanese.
The document was characterized by an unprecedented sharpness of its terms and the listing of numerous instances of violation of the "Open Door" principle by the Japanese Army and its puppet regimes.
Discarding usual diplomatic verbiage, the note openly declared that the "Japanese authorities are seeking to establish in areas which have come under Japanese military occupation general preferences for and superiority of, Japanese interests."
Among the instances of Japanese discrimination listed in the note was the unlawful interference with transportation of goods up the Yangtze River.
The earlier American note to the Japanese Government was delivered by Ambassador Grew on June 1 The note informed the Japanese that their "infringement of and interference with American rights in China" was "giving the Government of the United States increasing concern."

Restrictions Protested
The note further pointed out that while Japanese civilians have been permitted to enter and do business in areas from which the Sino-Japanese conflict has moved on American businessmen have been denied the same rights.
The Japanese reply Monday gave five reasons for not reopening the Yangtze as demanded by the three Powers.
The Japanese maintained that free navigation on the river would greatly interfere with Japanese military operations in upper Yangtze which, they contended, are still continuing.
Another reason given was that the booms, erected by the Chinese forces, had not yet been sufficiently removed as to permit any other vessels to pass except Japanese war vessels.
The extensive activities of Chinese guerrillas on both banks of the Yangtze were also cited in support of the Japanese contention that the river was yet unsafe for free navigation.
The fact that foreign vessels might be hit by floating mines let loose by Chinese troops was given as another reason for keeping the river closed.

Mine Danger Stressed
And lastly, the replies asserted that it would take the Japanese considerable time to remove all the mines from the surface of the river.
While it is yet too early to predict what steps the foreign Powers would take concerning the Japanese refusal to their demands, British shipping circles in Shanghai had intimated that Great Britain might take retaliatory measures.
In an interview with THE CHINA PRESS on Aug. 8, representatives of British shipping interests here revealed that the British Government was giving consideration to the closure of all British ports to Japanese shipping.
It was understood at that time that support of this action would be given by other interested nations unless the Japanese would agree to reopen the Yangtze to foreign shipping.
Britain was among the first nations to negotiate regarding commercial traffic on the Yangtze.
It will be recalled that shortly after Vice-Admiral Sir Percy Noble had concluded his inspection tour to upper Yangtze, British authorities in Shanghai began pressing the Japanese for the reopening of the river to foreign shipping.

《字林西报》。
1938年11月16日

一家代理机构在回答一位潜在客户的询问时表示，溯江而上的航运一直相当规律。该潜在客户获悉，一艘船只已于周一上午离开上海。
所有报告均表明，日本船只（并非 exclusively 军舰）一直在长江上航行，西至九江，为至少是中国托运人运送货物。
这直接驳斥了日本官方的声明，即长江航行仅出于军事目的才可行。
日本政府在其回复英国、法国和美国最近要求重新向外国航运开放长江的照会中提出了这一主张。

美国照会措辞强硬
10月6日，美国驻东京大使约瑟夫·格鲁（Joseph Grew）将美国照会递交给时任首相兼代理外相的近卫文麿亲王（Prince Ayamaro Konoye）。这份照会是三份照会中措辞最为强硬的，也是美国发给日本的第二份照会。
该文件的特点是措辞空前严厉，并列举了日军及其傀儡政权多次违反“门户开放”原则的实例。
该照会摒弃了通常的外交辞令，公开宣称“日本当局正试图在处于日本军事占领下的地区建立对日本利益的普遍优待和优越地位。”
照会中列出的日本歧视行为实例包括非法干涉沿长江向上的货物运输。
此前美国致日本政府的照会由格鲁大使于6月1日递交。该照会通知日本方面，其“对中国美国权利的侵犯和干涉”正“引起美国政府日益增大的关切”。

抗议限制措施
照会进一步指出，虽然日本平民被允许进入中日冲突已转移的地区并进行商业活动，但美国商人却被剥夺了同样的权利。
日本方面周一的回复列出了不按照三个大国的要求重新开放长江的五点理由。
日方坚持认为，河上的自由航行将严重干扰日军在长江上游的军事行动，他们声称这些行动仍在继续。
给出的另一个理由是，中国军队设置的封锁线尚未充分清除，除日本军舰外，不允许任何其他船只通过。
长江两岸中国游击队的广泛活动也被引用来支持日方的主张，即该河流对于自由航行而言仍不安全。
外国船只可能遭到中国军队布放的水雷袭击的事实，被列为保持河流封闭的另一理由。

强调水雷危险
最后，回复中声称，日本需要相当长的时间才能清除河面上的所有水雷。
虽然目前预测外国列强将针对日本拒绝其要求采取何种步骤还为时过早，但上海的英国航运界暗示，英国可能会采取报复性措施。
8月8日，在接见《字林西报》记者时，在沪英国航运利益代表透露，英国政府正在考虑对所有英国港口关闭日本航运。
当时据悉，除非日本同意重新向外国航运开放长江，否则其他相关国家将支持这一行动。
英国是最早就长江商业通航进行谈判的国家之一。
人们记得，在珀西·诺布尔海军中将（Vice-Admiral Sir Percy Noble）结束对长江上游的视察后不久，驻上海的英国当局便开始向日本施压，要求重新向外国航运开放该河流。

CHINA PRESS.
SEP 8 1938
REGISTER
N D.

Foreign Firms In China Face Threat Of
Large-Scale Japanese Trade Invasion

Nippon Imports Between
January, July Rise By
880 Per Cent

American and British business firms today face the threat of being permanently relegated to a place of unimportance as the Japanese economic drive rapidly succeeds in taking away from them the major portion of import and export trade of North and Central China, figures collected by authoritative foreign investigators reveal.

These foreign trade experts agree that in the event that Japan should succeed in establishing her overlordship in China, legally and permanently, the rich China market is likely to be dominated completely by the Japanese, with foreign firms taking only the small "left-overs" in trade.

Backed By Figures

This conclusion on the part of the investigators is backed by the phenomenal rise in Japan's trade with China.

Close study of the figures shows that between January 1938 and July 1938, Japanese imports to occupied areas in China increased by 880 per cent. Export from Nipponese-occupied areas in China to Japan rose by 260 per cent during the same period.

U.S. Figures Drop

These figures also show that between January and July this year, American exports to China dropped by 5 per cent, while Chinese exports to the United States climbed by 55 per cent.

During the same period, British exports to China increased by 60 per cent, while Chinese exports to the British Empire rose by 40 per cent.

Trade On Up-Grade

A study made by experts reveals that during January and July, the total imports into China increased by 14 per cent, while exports from China climbed by 80 per cent.

Investigators emphasized that this optimistic picture regarding the recovery of China's foreign trade should be taken with a "grain of salt" because a sizable portion of goods imported into China is now still unsold.

Studying the July foreign trade figures geographically, investigators found that 65 per cent or some $19,679,000 of the import business in North China was in the hands of the Japanese. During the same month, North China exported $13,-

718,000 worth of goods or 56 per cent of the total exports to Japan.

June Trade Surveyed

In June, total Japanese imports to North China amounted to $25,900,-000 or 80 per cent of the total imports to this area. Exports to Japan from North China in June totaled $24,000,000, or 55 per cent of the aggregate North China exports.

Comparing July figures with those of June, investigators found that North China import trade had decreased by six per cent while the import trade had dropped by 18 per cent.

In East China, with Shanghai as the main port, imports from Japan for July totalled $5,856,000 or about 25 per cent of the aggregate imports of $24,732,000. Exports from East China to Japan amounted to $2,865,000 or some 15 per cent of the total exports of $20,194,000.

Year's Trade Analysed

To obtain a correct picture of how Japanese imports and exports are dominating the China market investigators compared trade figures for July, 1937, the last "normal trade month" before the war, and July this year.

This comparison shows that Japanese imports to China increased by 7 per cent. Exports to Japan

Great Gains Contrast
With Big Drop In U.S.,
British Trade

rose during this 12-month period by 71 per cent.

In sharp contrast with the rise in Japanese figures are the huge drops in American and British export and import trade.

U.S. Trade Slumps

From July, 1937 to July this year, the total amount of imports from the U.S.A. decreased by 50 per cent, while Chinese exports to America dropped by 55 per cent. The comparison also shows that imports into China from the British Empire dropped during the 12-month period by 55 per cent while exports to the British Empire decreased by 35 per cent.

The trade figures included in the analysis, the investigators emphasized, are adjusted to include not only direct shipments, but also cargo delivered and shipped through.

It was also pointed out that in studying imports from and exports to Japan, cargoes to and from Korea, Chosen and Manchuria are also included. Figures for the United States include also trade done with the Philippine Islands.

《字林西报》。
1938年9月8日
登记号
N D.

在华外资企业面临
大规模日本贸易入侵的威胁

一月至七月间
日本进口额增长
880%

权威外国调查人员收集的数据显示，随着日本经济攻势迅速成功夺走华北和华中大部分进出口贸易，美国和英国商业公司今天面临着被永久边缘化为无足轻重地位的危险。

这些外贸专家一致认为，如果日本成功在法律上和永久性地确立其对中国的霸权，富裕的中国市场很可能完全由日本人主导，外资企业只能在贸易中分得少量的“残羹剩饭”。

数据支持

调查人员的这一结论得到了日本对华贸易惊人增长的佐证。

仔细研究数据显示，1938年1月至1938年7月间，日本向中国占领区的进口增长了880%。同期，从中国日占区出口到日本的数额增长了260%。

美国数据下降

这些数据还显示，今年1月至7月间，美国对华出口下降了5%，而中国对美出口增长了55%。

同期，英国对华出口增长了60%，而中国对英帝国出口增长了40%。

贸易呈上升趋势

专家的一项研究显示，1月至7月期间，中国总进口增长了14%，而中国出口增长了80%。

调查人员强调，对于中国对外贸易复苏的这一乐观景象应持“保留态度”，因为目前仍有相当一部分进口到中国的货物尚未售出。

从地理角度研究7月份的外贸数据，调查人员发现，华北进口业务的65%（约19,679,000美元）掌握在日本人手中。同月，华北出口货物价值13,718,000美元，占对日总出口的56%。

六月贸易考察

6月份，日本对华北的总进口额为25,900,000美元，占该地区总进口的80%。6月华北对日出口总额为24,000,000美元，占华北总出口的55%。

比较7月与6月的数据，调查人员发现华北进口贸易下降了6%，而进口贸易下降了18%。（注：原文此处似有笔误，前后均称进口贸易，依原文译出）

在以上海为主要港口的华东地区，7月从日本的进口总额为5,856,000美元，约占24,732,000美元总进口额的25%。华东对日出口额为2,865,000美元，约占20,194,000美元总出口额的15%。

年度贸易分析

为了准确了解日本进出口如何主导中国市场，调查人员比较了战前最后一个“正常贸易月份”——1937年7月与今年7月的贸易数据。

这种比较显示，日本对华进口增长了7%。对日出口

巨大增益与
美英贸易大幅下滑
形成鲜明对比

在这12个月期间增长了71%。

与美国数据的上升形成鲜明对比的是，美国和英国的进出口贸易出现了巨大跌幅。

美国贸易暴跌

从1937年7月到今年7月，从美国的进口总额下降了50%，而中国对美出口下降了55%。比较还显示，在这12个月期间，从英帝国进口到中国的数额下降了55%，而对英帝国的出口下降了35%。

调查人员强调，分析中包含的贸易数据经过调整，不仅包括直接运输的货物，还包括经转运交付和运输的货物。

此外还指出，在研究从日本进口和向日本出口时，往返朝鲜（Chosen）和满洲的货物也包括在内。美国的数据还包括与菲律宾群岛进行的贸易。

NOV 1 1 1938

Time for Action :
Formulation of Plans Wanted

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—According to the "China
Hong List" 1938, there are 16 Cham-
bers of Commerce in Shanghai.
Now surely the time has arrived for
representatives or even the full Com-
mittees of these organizations to
meet to discuss the present situation
and formulate plans to place Shang-
hai in the position it was previous
to the outbreak of hostilities. Any
decisions could be forwarded by the
National Chambers to their Govern-
ment Representatives and thus have
unanimity which would be a help to
those who, we trust in the near
future, will be conducting negotia-
tions for a Settlement of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities.
Shortly, four points of vital in-
terest to trade, and to Shanghai in
general, which could be threshed out
are :
1. The immediate return to full
Municipal Control of the Northern
and Eastern Districts of Shanghai
without any conditions attaching
thereto.
2. The immediate re-establishment
of the Whangpoo Conservancy Board.
3. A revision of the Land Regula-
tions.
4. The setting up of a Boundary
Commission to adjust the Municipal
Boundaries with natural lines of
demarcation.
L. E. CANNING.
Shanghai, Nov. 10.

《北华捷报》，

1938年11月11日

行动之时：
亟需制定计划

致《北华捷报》编辑
先生，——根据1938年《中国行名录》（China Hong List），上海有16个商会。
现在确实是这些组织的代表甚至全体委员会召开会议讨论当前局势并制定计划，使上海恢复到敌对行动爆发前的地位的时候了。任何决定均可由各全国商会转达给其政府代表，从而达成一致意见，这将有助于那些我们相信在不久的将来将进行中日敌对行动解决谈判的人士。
简而言之，可以深入探讨的对贸易及上海整体至关重要的四点如下：

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 25 1938
Time For Action

THERE is no better time than the present for Shanghai's large community of Americans—and other foreigners are by no means excluded—to express boldly and pointedly their thoughts on the existing situation in this city and the Yangtse Valley. The situation has reached a stage where it is patently ridiculous, and any Japanese statements to the contrary should receive no consideration.

We say that Americans should take the lead in matters regarding the immediate removal of shackles on this city and its immediate area which are hindering the progress of all, not excluding the Japanese. We say that Americans should be in the vanguard because we believe that members of the American community, backed by Washington, are the most logical persons to bring this matter to a head. Behind their community today is a powerful organization, composed of keen, shrewd businessmen who are not lacking in political weight in the nation's capital.

We know that there is some talk on the matter at the present time, and understand that certain negotiations are under way. To them we give our support. We also want to sound a note of caution that compromises are only concessions—and we are of the opinion that concessions do not exactly dove-tail into the present policy of the American State Department.

A marked indication of the trend of thought among Americans here was heard on Friday night when the radio commentator of the China Weekly Review interviewed Mr. George H. Greene, President of the American Junior Chamber of Commerce. Mr. Greene, we have heard, accurately reflected the opinion of the majority of Shanghai's Americans.

Mr. Greene declared in the broadcasted interview: "Obviously what is holding up trade, is the closure of markets in the interior because Japanese are in occupation of the territory along the Yangtse River and are preventing the ingress of ships and the return of businessmen to their stations in the interior.

"At the same time, Japanese are freely importing their goods and are permitting their own businessmen to go in, thus creating a monopoly for their own benefit. Shanghai, of course, depends on a volume of through trade for its prosperity, and normal conditions will not return until foreign ships call at this port and markets are reopened in the interior," he observed.

Last week, THE CHINA PRESS published an interview with Mr. C. Agaki, Special Japanese Deputy Commissioner of Police, who pointed out the complete lack of expression by foreigners concerning matters of trade. We view his remark as a challenge to all foreigners to speak up. More comment like the Junior Chamber's leader is needed.

行动之时

对于上海庞大的美国人群体——其他外侨也绝非被排除在外——而言，现在正是就本市及长江流域的现存局势大胆而明确地表达其想法的最佳时机。局势已发展到显然荒谬的地步，任何与此相悖的日本声明都不应予以考虑。

我们认为，美国人应在立即解除束缚本市及其周边地区、阻碍各方（包括日本人在内）进展的枷锁方面发挥带头作用。我们主张美国人应处于先锋地位，因为我们相信，在华盛顿的支持下，美国社区成员是推动此事达到关键阶段的最合适人选。如今，支持该社区的是一个强大的组织，由敏锐、精明的商人组成，他们在国家首都拥有不容小觑的政治分量。

我们知道目前对此事有一些议论，并获悉某些谈判正在进行中。我们对此表示支持。同时，我们也想发出警告：妥协仅仅是让步——而且我们认为，让步与美国国务院当前的政策并不完全契合。

上周五晚，《密勒氏评论报》电台评论员采访美国青年商会主席乔治·H·格林（George H. Greene）先生时，人们听到了在沪美国人思想趋势的一个显著标志。据我们所知，格林先生准确反映了上海大多数美国人的意见。

格林先生在广播采访中宣称：“显然，阻碍贸易的是内地市场的关闭，因为日本人占领了长江沿线地区，阻止船只进入和商人返回其在内地的驻地。

“与此同时，日本人自由进口他们的商品，并允许他们自己的商人进入，从而为他们自己的利益创造垄断。当然，上海的繁荣依赖于大量的过境贸易，只有当外国船只停靠本港且内地市场重新开放时，正常状况才会恢复，”他指出。

上周，《字林西报》刊登了对日本警务处特别副总监赤木（C. Agaki，音译）先生的采访，他指出外侨在贸易事务上完全缺乏发声。我们将他的言论视为对所有外侨挺身直言的挑战。我们需要更多像这位青年商会领袖那样的评论。
